# Sourdough: everything in one file

> Sourdough bakes all five Wayne State app shapes: raw PHP, raw PHP + Vue, Laravel + Blade, Laravel + Blade + Vue islands and Laravel + Inertia/Vue, each with SESAME sign-in, HELMET headers, PROCTOR, Preflight CI and Squire's deploy files already in it.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/README.md

## Sourdough

**Feed it and it grows.**

A starter you feed: `sourdough new` makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Every loaf gets proofed before it ships.

Documentation: the [docs site](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html) is built from [`docs/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/) by Squire's docs builder; `composer docs:build` rebuilds it and `composer docs:check` fails when it is stale. The docs pages wear the front page's header, menu, palette and fonts: edit [`docs/_header.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/_header.html) and [`docs/theme/sourdough.css`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/theme/sourdough.css) (named by the `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`), never the kit's `docs.css`.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.

On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/sourdough) on git.wayne.edu. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it. git.wayne.edu is the starter culture now; GitHub is the slice Packagist eats.

Sourdough is the app starter for the WSU stack, and it starts every app shape: raw PHP, raw PHP with a Vue SPA, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade and Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue. WELD is that last shape already built from it. One command scaffolds a new app with WayneUI (the interface), SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), Pinstripe (coding standard), PROCTOR (checks), the Preflight CI components, Squire's deploy files and ADVISOR (the stack's MCP server) already in place, with its PHP floor read from CREED's policy. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Install

```
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

After `composer global require`, the `sourdough` command lives in `composer global config bin-dir --absolute`; put that directory on your PATH.

Or scaffold without installing, with `composer create-project waynestate/sourdough`.

### Usage

```
sourdough new [dir] [options]
```

`dir` is the directory to create the app in. It is required unless you use `--describe`.

Options:

- `--raw` use the raw PHP base
- `--laravel` use the Laravel base
- `--vue` add a Vue front end
- `--inertia` use Inertia/Vue (implies `--laravel`)
- `--sail` run the Laravel app on Sail for local work: compose.yaml and laravel/sail in require-dev, MySQL 8.4 LTS; needs WSL2 on Windows, where `--docker` is the route that works natively
- `--docker` generate a Dockerfile and compose.yaml for local work (native on every OS; amd64 and arm64): the app's own base images, pinned by digest, are the single place to swap in Squire's Citadel-parity image when it exists; MySQL 8.4; Playbook credentials reach the build only as a BuildKit secret, never a build arg
- `--dry-run` print the plan and write nothing
- `--name` app name (default: the basename of ``)
- `--no-input` never prompt (Sourdough has no prompts)
- `--json` with `--dry-run`, print the plan as JSON
- `--describe ""` describe what the app does; a model plans it (needs the `SOURDOUGH_LLM_*` env vars)
- `--plan-only` with `--describe`, print the plan as JSON and write nothing
- `--plan ` a ready-made plan file (JSON, or YAML ending in `.yaml` or `.yml`, matching `resources/plan.schema.json`), such as the `.sourdough/plan.yaml` every bake saves
- `--playbook` kept for compatibility: Playbook is now the default
- `--no-playbook` skip the Playbook wiring (for CI and automated tests only; WSU apps need Playbook)
- `--no-advisor` skip the ADVISOR wiring (no `require-dev` entry, no `.mcp.json` git-ignore line of its own, no README section; the Laravel shapes still ignore `/.mcp.json` for Laravel Boost)

Exit codes: `0` done, `1` refused (invalid flags, non-empty target, not available, model gave up), `2` tool error.

By default the generated app requires `waynestate/playbook` (WSU's private shared-values package on git.wayne.edu): the VCS repository, the package in `require`, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends your token to git.wayne.edu, the seven setting names in `.env.example`, a `composer playbook` script that shows whether Playbook is installed, and a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section that explains how to get read access. Before writing anything, `sourdough new` checks that this machine can read the package (a Composer credential, then a direct git probe); without read access it refuses with exit `1` and prints the how-to, and if it cannot reach git.wayne.edu it still generates the app but warns that `composer install` will need the connection. Non-interactive runs and CI environments skip the check. `--dry-run` runs the check but never refuses, and its JSON plan carries a `playbook` key with the mode, the access status and the probe that answered. After generation the Next steps point at `composer playbook`. `--playbook` is kept for compatibility and changes nothing; `--no-playbook` skips all of it. The two flags together are refused with exit `1`.

Generated apps ship with ADVISOR wired in by default: `waynestate/advisor` lands in `require-dev`, `.mcp.json` is git-ignored (a client config starts a program for whoever opens the project), and the README gains an "ADVISOR" section. The Next steps print the install line once dependencies are in:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
```

`--no-advisor` skips all of it.

The three Laravel shapes also ship Laravel Boost as a dev-only tool, whatever the ADVISOR answer: `laravel/boost` in `require-dev`, a guarded `composer boost-update` after `composer update`, a `.gitignore` block for what `php artisan boost:install` writes (`/.mcp.json`, `/boost.json`, `/CLAUDE.md`, `/AGENTS.md`, `/.claude/skills/`, `/.junie/`), the stack's guidelines and two starter rules in `.ai/`, and `tests/Feature/BoostDevOnlyTest.php`. ADVISOR complements Boost: Boost knows Laravel, ADVISOR knows the stack. See [Laravel Boost, dev only](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/laravel.md#laravel-boost-dev-only).

The app name (from `--name`, from the plan, or from the basename of ``) must start with a letter or number and use only letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores, at most 63 characters; anything else is refused before anything is written.

### Permutations

| Flags | Permutation |
|---|---|
| (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

All five permutations bake: raw PHP since 0.1.0, the three Laravel shapes since 0.1.5 and raw PHP + Vue since 0.1.6. `--raw --vue` is the raw PHP bake with a Vue 3 front end over it: PHP answers JSON under `/api/`, Vite builds the Vue app, and `src/Vite.php` loads it from the build or the dev server.

Every bake takes its PHP floor from CREED's policy, not from a number baked into the template: the oldest PHP line still supported a year after the policy's refresh date (raised to what the Laravel major needs) becomes `require.php`, `config.platform.php` and the start of the CI test matrix. If the policy cannot be read, the bake falls back to the pinned `^8.3` and says so. `sourdough new` prints both a `PHP:` line and a `Support:` line, and every shape has an owner, a support window and a sunset path, so no starter goes stale on the counter. The rules are in [Support and sunset](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/support.md).

Oracle is wired but dormant in every generated app. The settings `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT`, `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME` ship commented out in `.env.example`; while they are empty, nothing connects and nothing errors. Once you fill them in, Laravel apps check the wiring with `php artisan oracle:check`, and raw PHP apps run queries through the `App\Oracle` helper, which takes values only as binds and answers mistakes with plain sentences. The Laravel shapes require `yajra/laravel-oci8` and declare `ext-oci8` 3.4.1 as a platform package, so the driver is ready the day the settings are filled in: most WSU apps need Oracle, and Citadel's images carry oci8 and Instant Client. The command finds the check file where it lives: `oracle-check.php` at the app root, where Squire's Laravel layout ships it, first, then `deploy/oracle-check.php`.

### Describe a plan

Instead of choosing flags, describe what the app does and let a model plan it:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments"
```

Sourdough asks an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan, validates it against `resources/plan.schema.json`, and prints it. The model kneads the dough, but you decide when the loaf is ready to bake: if the answer is not valid JSON, does not match the schema, or the model gives up after one retry, Sourdough refuses with a message pointing you to `--plan=` (exit `1`). You write the plan yourself and pass it in.

To see the plan as JSON without writing anything:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments" --plan-only
```

`--describe` stops at the plan: baking straight from a description is not built yet. Save the plan to a file and pass it with `--plan`, which bakes it:

```
sourdough new my-app --plan plan.json
```

`--plan` reads the file, validates it against the schema, and continues the normal generation flow using the plan's permutation and name. A file ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` is read as YAML; anything else as JSON.

Every bake saves its plan in the app as `.sourdough/plan.yaml`: the recipe card taped inside the jar's lid. A `--plan` bake saves that plan (with `--name`, if you gave one); a bake from flags saves the shape, the name and all four parts. The card is a valid plan file, so `sourdough new other-app --plan=my-app/.sourdough/plan.yaml` bakes the same loaf again. See [Plan format](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/plan-format.md#the-saved-plan).

#### Model configuration

`--describe` needs three environment variables (no defaults, no key in code):

- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_BASE_URL` the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including the API path (usually `/v1`)
- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` the API key
- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_MODEL` the model name

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works: a hosted API, a local server, or WarriorGPT. Sourdough does not care about the hostname; it only needs the base URL, key, and model.

A plan is a small JSON object:

```json
{
    "permutation": "raw",
    "parts": ["sesame", "helmet"],
    "name": "my-app",
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "Post",
            "fields": [
                { "name": "title", "type": "string" },
                { "name": "body", "type": "text" }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "pages": ["/", "/posts"]
}
```

`permutation`, `parts`, and `name` are required; `models` and `pages` are optional. `parts` is a subset of `sesame`, `helmet`, `proctor`, and `preflight`.

### The manifest

Every app Sourdough generates carries a `.sourdough/manifest.json` recording what was generated: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 hash of every file, each marked `managed` (Sourdough owns it and will update it) or `seeded` (Sourdough wrote it once and you own it now: `.env.example`, `README.md`, and `package-lock.json` on the shapes with a front end).

The manifest is the starter's memory: it remembers what went into the loaf, so `feed` knows what to refresh and what to leave to rise on its own. `sourdough feed` reads it to bring template updates into your app without clobbering what you've changed.

`sourdough manifest --check` lists the managed files that have drifted from the manifest:

```
sourdough manifest --check
```

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` a managed file changed or is missing, `2` tool error (no manifest, or no `--check`). Seeded files are never reported. They're yours.

Commit the manifest. It's the record that keeps `feed` honest.

Next to it sits `.sourdough/plan.yaml`, the plan the app was baked from. It is not in the manifest, so it is neither managed nor seeded: `feed` and `manifest --check` never read, rewrite or flag it, and you may edit it as the app grows. Commit it too.

### Feeding an app

`sourdough feed` brings template updates into an app made with `sourdough new`, without clobbering what you've changed. Install the new Sourdough, then, in the app, on a clean git tree:

```
sourdough feed --dry-run
sourdough feed
```

Feed bakes your app's shape again with the answers in its manifest, then goes file by file:

- a file the template did not change is left alone, whatever you did to it;
- a managed file you never touched takes the template's new version;
- a file you both changed is three-way merged by git (`git merge-file`), from the version Sourdough wrote last time; where you both changed the same lines, git's conflict markers go in the file (`<<<<<<< app` and `>>>>>>> sourdough `), never a silent overwrite;
- new template files are added, and files the template dropped are removed only if you never changed them;
- a file that already matches the template's new version is only recorded in the manifest (`record`); that is also how an app baked by 0.1.6 with `--sail` or `--docker` gets its oven into the manifest;
- seeded files (`README.md`, `.env.example`, `package-lock.json`) are never touched.

Then the manifest moves to the new base, and the template's version of each managed file you've changed is kept in `.sourdough/base/`, so the next feed can merge from it even when git history can't. Commit both.

Exit codes: `0` fed cleanly (or nothing to feed), `1` fed with conflicts to resolve, `2` tool error (no manifest, no git, a dirty tree, conflicts left from the last feed, a manifest from a newer Sourdough). With `--dry-run` nothing is written: `0` the app is fresh, `1` feeding would change files. Every shape's pipeline runs it in a `sourdough-feed` job, next to `sourdough manifest --check`: an app that falls behind its template gets a warning (never a blocked deploy), hand edits to managed files are listed, and a broken record fails the job. `--json` prints the plan for machines.

Feed needs git and nothing else: git is the merge engine and the undo button (`git restore . && git clean -fd`). The Laravel shapes bake on a fresh `laravel/laravel` skeleton, so feeding one needs Composer and the network, the same as `sourdough new`; skeleton updates arrive as template updates. The full story is in [Keeping apps current](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/keeping-current.md). A fed starter is a happy starter.

The deploy files in your app (`build.sh`, `scripts/release.sh`, the `.squire/` config, and their friends) come from Squire's exported copy, checked into this repository at `templates/squire/`. The copy is Squire 0.10.0's kit, so a Laravel release first refuses to run with no `APP_KEY` or with `APP_DEBUG` on in production (and warns when `APP_ENV` is not production), then `scripts/release.sh` asks PROCTOR's deploy gate (`proctor gate`, graded on the PHP that runs the release; `SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME` names another or `skip`) for a go or no-go before the frontend build and the migrations, keeps the verdict in `storage/squire/` (`SQUIRE_PROCTOR_RECORD_DIR`) as the next release's baseline, and after the optimize step restarts Laravel's long-lived processes (`php artisan reload`, or `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt` on an older Laravel; report only, `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0` turns it off). The image hardens too: the web's PHP loses its shell functions (`SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS` sets the list), opcache runs with production settings (`SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE`), Apache answers `ServerTokens Prod`, and secrets can be read from `/run/secrets`. Squire owns them; Sourdough installs them as-is and records them in the manifest, so you never edit them by hand. To refresh them, run `composer squire-copy:sync`, which rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package, then verify it with `composer squire-copy:check` (part of `composer ci`).

### Which command when

Several stack commands sound alike (`weld:doctor`, `squire doctor`, `proctor check`) and do different jobs. Find your question in the second column and run the command beside it. The doctors look at setup, the proctor grades against policy, and the gate decides deploys: same waiting room, different appointments.

| Command | What it checks | When to run it | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `composer ci` | **Will my pipeline pass?** The repo's own CI contract, the same command the pipeline runs: validation, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, `composer audit` and whatever checks the repo adds. | Before every push. | App repo, CI |
| `bin/weld.sh doctor` or `.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor` (both run `php artisan weld:doctor`) | **Does my WELD app hold together?** The app key, writable `storage` and `bootstrap/cache`, the database connection and pending migrations. One PASS, WARN or FAIL line each; exit 1 on a FAIL. Standards are PROCTOR's. | After `up`, when the app will not start, and after every deploy off Citadel. | App repo (in the app container), deploy host (in the app container) |
| `vendor/bin/squire doctor` | **Is my Citadel release setup right?** `build.sh`, the release scripts, the health check, script hygiene, line endings, secrets kept out of git and the local parity setup, against Squire's rules. Exit 1 on a failed rule. The lock file, audit and MySQL 5.6 checks are handed to PROCTOR. | After `squire init` or `squire update`, and before the first deploy. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/squire init --check` | **Have the files Squire wrote drifted from its templates?** Missing, outdated or edited copies. Writes nothing; exit 1 on drift. | After you upgrade Squire (then run `squire update`), and in CI. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle`, or `php artisan oracle:check` in WELD and Sourdough's Laravel apps | **Can my app reach Oracle?** The `ORACLE_*` settings, the host, the port, the `oci8` driver and the login, in plain language, printing setting names and never values. Silent when the app has no Oracle settings. | After you fill in the `ORACLE_*` settings, or when a connection fails. Squire's `release.sh` runs the same check on every release, as a report. | App repo, deploy host |
| `vendor/bin/proctor check` (`composer proctor` in WELD and Sourdough's apps) | **Does my app meet CREED's policy?** The PHP floor, Laravel, Node and MySQL end of life, the committed lock, `composer audit`, open-ended constraints, portability, MySQL 5.6 safety, overrides and the rest of its checks. Exit 1 on a FAIL. | Before you merge; the pipeline runs it too. | App repo, CI |
| `vendor/bin/proctor gate` | **May this commit deploy?** The deploy-time subset of `proctor check`, ratcheted against the last release's verdict, so a deploy that makes nothing worse goes. Exit 1 is a no-go. | At deploy time. Squire's `release.sh` calls it for you. | Deploy host |
| `sourdough manifest --check` | **Which managed files did I change since Sourdough baked my app?** Managed files that changed or are missing against `.sourdough/manifest.json`; seeded files are yours and never reported. Exit 1 on a change. | Before `sourdough feed`. | App repo, CI |
| `sourdough feed --dry-run` | **Is my app behind its Sourdough template?** The plan a feed would apply, with nothing written. Exit 1 when feeding would change files. | After you install a new Sourdough, and in CI to catch an app falling behind. | App repo, CI |
| `booster plan` | **What does my upgrade take?** The ordered PHP, Laravel and front-end hops, the dependencies that block them, and advisory PHPCompatibility and PHPStan scans. Changes nothing. | Before an upgrade, and when PROCTOR says your PHP or Laravel is past support. | App repo |
| `booster replay check` | **Does my app still answer the same after a change?** Replays the requests in `booster-replay.json` and compares the answers with the ones `booster replay record` saved. Exit 1 on a changed answer. | After an upgrade hop or a hand fix, once you have a recording. | App repo (in Docker) |
| `booster init --check` | **Are Booster's coding-tab playbooks current?** The playbooks in `.agents/skills`. Changes nothing; exit 1 when one is missing or out of date. | After you upgrade Booster, and in CI. | App repo, CI |
| `php bin/regen-check.php --generated ` | **Is WELD still Sourdough's Inertia shape?** WELD, file by file, against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia`; fails only on drift that `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` does not already accept. | When Sourdough's Inertia shape or WELD changes. | WELD repo, CI |
| `rollcall report` | **Where does the whole fleet stand?** The latest scan's totals against CREED's policy: PHP, Laravel, the auth package, PROCTOR results and the end-of-life burn-down. Always exit 0; it never gates. | After `rollcall scan`, on the scan's schedule. | CI (a scheduled scan job) |

The canonical copy of this table is in WELD's docs: [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html).

### Testing

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

From the repo root:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2 composer validate --strict
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli php bin/sourdough new /tmp/demo --dry-run
```

The `stack-composer-cache` volume keeps Composer's downloads between runs; Docker creates it the first time. The smoke gate bakes a shape for real and runs the generated app's own checks; see the "Smoke gate" section of [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md) for the full recipe. On Windows, `.\scripts\smoke-shape.ps1 ` runs it in one line.

The proof harness runs that gate on every shape and every Laravel shape in each oven, one after another in Docker: it bakes each with this checkout, checks the manifest, feeds a bake of the last release forward, installs the app, runs its own suite, PROCTOR and `composer ci`, then boots it and fetches its front page. `sh scripts/proof.sh` on Linux and macOS, `.\scripts\proof.ps1` on Windows. What each run proves, and the Last run table, are on the [Proof](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/proof.md) page.

The site accessibility gate runs Preflight's own a11y checker (vendored in `tools/a11y/check.mjs` from the 0.4.0 tag CI pins, held there by `tests/A11yCheckerPinTest.php`) over every page under `site/` in Docker, in light and dark at 320 px and 1280 px with the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow check: `sh scripts/a11y.sh` from Git Bash, Linux or macOS, `scripts\a11y.ps1` on Windows. It uses the same image and inputs as the a11y job in CI, so a page that passes here passes the pipeline.

#### Tests in the apps it bakes

The Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade + Vue islands, Inertia) come with Pest 4. The skeleton's PHPUnit example keeps running, `composer test` and `composer ci` run Pest, and the baked tests read `.env` when it exists, otherwise `.env.example`, on top of `phpunit.xml`. Their `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs the php-test matrix with `vendor/bin/pest` too, because PHPUnit refuses to load Pest files. Production refuses to boot on the tests' dummy `APP_KEY` (`app/Support/DummyAppKey.php`). The raw PHP shape is unchanged. Write new tests in Pest.

### CI

Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner.

Every baked `.gitlab-ci.yml` caches its downloads: Docker Hub images come through the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy
when the GitLab has one (`IMAGE_PREFIX`, Docker Hub otherwise), and Composer and npm installs are cached per lock
file. See [Dependency caching](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/ci.md#dependency-caching).

Every baked pipeline also carries three gates from Preflight: an accessibility check of the app's own pages
(signed in, at WCAG 2.2 AA, blocking), a CycloneDX bill of materials for Composer and, in the front-end shapes, npm,
and Gitleaks over the repository. A `.deploy` template keeps any deploy job on protected refs, and each generated
README lists the GitLab settings a file cannot hold. See [CI](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/HEAD/docs/guides/ci.md#the-accessibility-gate).

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/

A starter for Wayne State apps

## Sourdough

Feed it and it grows.

![Sourdough logo: a starter jar whose starter has risen into a dome, well above the gold band that marks where it began](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/brand/sourdough-avatar-512.png)

Hungry. It has not been fed yet today.

`sourdough new` makes a Wayne State app with the stack already in it: SESAME for sign-in, HELMET for the security headers, PROCTOR and Preflight for the checks, and Squire's files for deploying to Citadel. With no flags that's a raw PHP app, and you add WayneUI's standalone file with one download. All five shapes bake today, from raw PHP to Inertia.

The whole recipe

```
$ composer global require waynestate/sourdough
$ sourdough new my-app
```

**Want Laravel with Inertia and Vue?** Sourdough bakes it with `--inertia`. [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) is that shape already built, with the stack's product docs and site on top.

[Start baking](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/#start-title) [See the five loaves](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/#loaves-title)

Proofing log

### The proof

What goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`.

1. 08:00 **Mix.** `sourdough new` picks the shape; with no flags that's raw PHP.
2. 08:20 **Flour: WayneUI.** The interface, from WayneUI's standalone PHP file, which you download once.
3. 08:40 **Water: SESAME.** Sign-in. A fake driver locally, CAS in production.
4. 09:00 **Salt: HELMET.** Security headers, a hardened session, and `/up` for the load balancer.
5. 10:30 **Levain: PROCTOR.** The standards check. Preflight's CI components run it on every push, along with the tests, a Composer audit, an accessibility check of your own pages, a bill of materials and a secret scan.
6. 13:00 **Doubled.** Well past the gold band. A label goes on: `.sourdough/manifest.json`.
7. 14:00 **Divide and shape.** Cut into the five shapes the stack supports, every one of them ready to bake.

On the cooling rack

### Five loaves, one starter

These are the five app shapes the stack supports, and all five bake today. The proof harness bakes, boots and feeds forward every one of them: read [the latest proof](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html). Score a loaf to see what's inside.

Country boule

#### Raw PHP

Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path. No framework, no build.

Out of the oven since 0.1.0

`sourdough new my-app --raw`

The crumb

- `public/index.php` HELMET boots first, then SESAME signs you in
- `composer.json` helmet, sesame and Playbook, with pinstripe, proctor and advisor for dev
- `pint.json` and `phpstan.neon` Pinstripe's standard: Pint on the per preset, PHPStan at level 8
- `.gitlab-ci.yml` Preflight components: PROCTOR, tests on PHP 8.3 to 8.5, audit, accessibility, SBOM and a secret scan, plus a `sourdough-feed` job
- `build.sh` and `scripts/release.sh` Squire's Citadel deploy files
- `.env.example` and `README.md` seeded: yours from day one
- `.sourdough/manifest.json` the label on the jar

Bâtard

#### Raw PHP + Vue

A Vue single-page app over JSON, on raw PHP. No framework, one build.

Out of the oven since 0.1.6

`sourdough new my-app --raw --vue`

The crumb

- `public/index.php` the raw boot, then JSON under `/api/` and one page for Vue
- `resources/js/App.vue` drawn with WayneUI's Vue components, pinned at 2.0.8
- `src/Vite.php` reads Vite's manifest, nonces every tag for HELMET
- Next steps: `composer install`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, `composer serve`

Baguette

#### Laravel + Blade

The classic Wayne State shape: Laravel with Blade views.

Out of the oven since 0.1.5

`sourdough new my-app --laravel`

The crumb

A fresh Laravel skeleton from Composer with the stack wired in: SESAME through the Laravel adapter, HELMET's config, `/up` for liveness and `/ready` that asks the database, the cache and the scheduler, Pest 4, Laravel Boost for dev, PROCTOR and Preflight in CI, Squire's Laravel deploy files and the manifest. Oracle's `oci8` driver is required and waits, dormant, for its settings. Next steps: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `php artisan serve`.

Seeded loaf

#### Laravel + Blade + Vue islands

Blade pages with Vue islands, like seeds in the crust.

Out of the oven since 0.1.5

`sourdough new my-app --laravel --vue`

The crumb

The Laravel + Blade bake under a front-end layer: Vite with the Vue plugin, and a `resources/js/app.js` registry that mounts a Vue 3 app on every `[data-vue-island]` element. Next steps add `npm install` and `npm run build` before `php artisan serve`.

Tin loaf

#### Laravel + Inertia/Vue

Laravel with Inertia and Vue, as one app.

Out of the oven since 0.1.5

`sourdough new my-app --inertia`

The crumb

Laravel with Inertia and Vue as one app: Inertia pages rendered by Vue, Ziggy routes, the stack packages, Squire's Laravel deploy files and the manifest. [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) is this shape already built, with the stack's product docs and site on top; you can also bake it yourself with `--inertia`.

Not sure yet? `sourdough new my-app --dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing. It works with every shape's flags.

Recipe card No. 1

### What's baked in

Baker's percentages, roughly. The parts are Composer packages, so `composer update` updates them. Only the code that connects them lives in the template.

**The parts of the stack in every Sourdough app, as ingredients**

| Ingredient | Part | What it does in your app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100% Flour | [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) | The interface: WayneUI's standalone PHP file, fetched once into `public/`. |
| 75% Water | [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/) | Sign-in. The fake driver in development; the cas driver in production, with `SESAME_CAS_URL` and `SESAME_SERVICE_URL`. |
| 2% Salt | [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) | The runtime baseline: security headers, session cookie flags, trusted proxies from `HELMET_PROXIES`, and `/up` answering `200 ok`. The Laravel shapes add `/ready`, which answers 503 while the database, the cache or the scheduler is down. |
| 20% Levain | [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) | The standards check. CI runs `vendor/bin/proctor check` on every push. The release script asks `proctor gate` for a go or no-go too, as a report unless you set `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`. |
| 1 Oven | [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/) | CI from `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to Preflight 0.4.0: PROCTOR, tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, a Composer audit, an accessibility check of your own pages at WCAG 2.2 AA that blocks, a bill of materials and a Gitleaks secret scan. |
| 1 Recipe | [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/) | The rules the loaf is judged by. Every bake reads its PHP floor from CREED's policy, and PROCTOR grades the app against the same file. |
| 1 Basket | Release script | `build.sh` and `scripts/release.sh` come from Squire and run on Citadel at build and release time. Off Citadel, the app reads the same environment variables on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker. |
| 1 Pinch | [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/) | For your AI assistant: the stack's MCP server, in `require-dev`, answers from the stack's own docs. `--no-advisor` leaves it out. |

Bake at `composer serve` until golden.

Pinned above the bench

### Feeding schedule

A starter you never feed goes flat. Every app Sourdough makes carries `.sourdough/manifest.json`: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers you chose, and a sha256 of every file. That's how `sourdough feed` knows which files it can update, and which ones you've kneaded.

1. Bake day
   `sourdough new my-app`
   Makes the app and writes the manifest. Commit the manifest with the rest of the app.
2. Any day
   `sourdough manifest --check`
   Is it still alive? Lists every managed file that has drifted from the manifest. Run it in the app any time; every shape's pipeline runs it too, in the `sourdough-feed` job, and only lists what drifted.
   - **0**: clean
   - **1**: a managed file changed or is missing
   - **2**: no manifest, or no `--check`
3. Feeding
   `sourdough feed`
   Brings template updates into your app without clobbering what you changed. It bakes your shape again and lets git do a three-way merge, file by file; where you both changed the same lines, it leaves git's conflict markers for you instead of guessing. Run `--dry-run` first; every shape's pipeline runs it too, and warns when a feed is due.
   - **0**: fed (or already fresh)
   - **1**: fed, with conflicts to resolve
   - **2**: no manifest, no git, or a dirty tree

#### Managed we keep feeding these

- `public/index.php`
- `composer.json`
- `.gitlab-ci.yml`
- Squire's deploy files: `build.sh`, `scripts/`, `deployments/`, `.squire/`
- `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`

#### Seeded written once, yours now

- `.env.example`
- `README.md`
- `package-lock.json`

The lock comes only with a front end. Seeded files are never reported. They're yours to knead.

Quick start

### Your first loaf

Sourdough is one PHP command, so the steps match on every system; only the shell changes. You need PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer.

**Windows**

PowerShell

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl.exe -o public/wayne-ui.php https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
composer serve
```

**macOS**

Terminal (zsh)

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
composer serve
```

**Linux**

bash

```
# 1. Get the starter
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
# 2. Bake the app
sourdough new my-app
cd my-app
# 3. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once
curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php
# 4. Install and serve
composer install
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
composer serve
```

ADVISOR answers questions about the stack from inside your AI assistant; skip it with `sourdough new --no-advisor`.

To move to a newer WayneUI release, change the version in the URL above and run the fetch again.

**`sourdough` not found?** Add the folder that `composer global config bin-dir --absolute` prints to your PATH. Then open `http://localhost:8000`: locally the app signs in with SESAME's fake driver.

Hand it to your agent

### Recipes for your agent

Three prompts for whatever coding agent you use. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each tells the agent what Sourdough put in the app and what it must leave alone, and each tells it to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with Sourdough

Installs Sourdough, makes a raw PHP app with WayneUI, serves it locally and runs the manifest check.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer bake a new app with Sourdough, the app starter of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Sourdough bakes all five shapes: raw PHP on WayneUI's standalone path (--raw or no flag), raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON (--raw --vue), Laravel + Blade (--laravel), Laravel + Blade + Vue islands (--laravel --vue) and Laravel + Inertia/Vue (--inertia). Each comes with SESAME (sign-in), HELMET (security headers and the /up check), Pinstripe (coding standard), PROCTOR (checks), the Preflight CI components and Squire's deploy files already in it.

Read first:
- https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Sourdough's pages, each one as Markdown; llms-full.txt beside it holds the README too. Fetch what you need; do not work from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: get_project_status and read_project_docs for sourdough answer from the stack's own docs, and policy_lookup gives today's PHP support from CREED. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Check that PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer are on the PATH, and say which versions you found.
2. Install the starter with `composer global require waynestate/sourdough`. If the sourdough command is then not found, add the folder that `composer global config bin-dir --absolute` prints to the PATH.
3. Bake the app with `sourdough new my-app --raw`, using the folder name I give you in place of my-app, and change into it.
4. Fetch WayneUI's standalone file once. Windows (PowerShell): `curl.exe -o public/wayne-ui.php https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php`. macOS and Linux: `curl -o public/wayne-ui.php https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/v2/releases/2.0.8/wayne-ui.php`.
5. Run `composer install`, then wire in ADVISOR with `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write`, then `composer serve`, and tell me to open http://localhost:8000. Locally SESAME signs in with its fake driver.
6. Run `sourdough manifest --check` in the app and report what it says.

Constraints:
- Sourdough bakes all five shapes: raw PHP (--raw or no flag), raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON (--raw --vue), Laravel + Blade (--laravel), Laravel + Blade + Vue islands (--laravel --vue) and Laravel + Inertia/Vue (--inertia). A --raw --vue app needs npm install and npm run build before composer serve shows the page. WELD is the Inertia/Vue shape already built, with the stack's product docs and site on top: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- .sourdough/manifest.json records every file Sourdough wrote. Managed files are Sourdough's; .env.example and README.md are seeded and mine. Commit the manifest.
- The deploy files (build.sh, scripts/release.sh, the .squire/ config) come from Squire. Never edit them by hand.
- Never commit .env, and never paste a secret into a prompt or a file.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess: a folder name, a PHP version you cannot read, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: what you ran and what it said, the app's files one level deep, then your questions.
```

#### Check what has drifted in a Sourdough app

Lists the managed files that changed since Sourdough wrote them, shows what a feed would bring in, and suggests what to put back. It changes nothing.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent checking an app that Sourdough baked, at Wayne State University. Sourdough is the app starter of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Every app it bakes carries .sourdough/manifest.json: the Sourdough version, the template, the answers chosen, and a sha256 hash of every file it wrote, each marked managed or seeded.

Read first:
- https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then llms-full.txt beside it: the README's manifest section says what managed and seeded mean.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sourdough and squire, and run_proctor_check for this app. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- .sourdough/manifest.json, composer.json and public/index.php in this app.

Task:
1. Run `sourdough manifest --check` at the app's root. Exit 0 is clean, 1 means a managed file changed or is missing, 2 is a tool error.
2. For each file it reports, say what changed, as far as you can tell, and whether it looks deliberate.
3. If ADVISOR is connected, call run_proctor_check for this app and list the findings.
4. Run `sourdough feed --dry-run` and list what a feed would update, merge, add, remove or leave in conflict. Exit 0 means fresh, 1 means feeding would change files, 2 is a tool error.
5. Change nothing. For each drifted file, propose whether to put it back or keep the change, and why. A kept change is fine: feed merges it with the template's.

Constraints:
- Seeded files (.env.example and README.md) are mine and never count as drift.
- The deploy files come from Squire, through Sourdough. Never hand-edit them to make a check pass.
- Never run sourdough feed without --dry-run unless I say so: a real feed writes files.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: a table (file, managed or seeded, state, deliberate or not), the PROCTOR findings, then your proposals and your questions.
```

#### Bake a Laravel app with Sourdough

Installs Sourdough, bakes one of the three Laravel shapes, serves it locally and runs the manifest check.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer bake a new Laravel app with Sourdough, the app starter of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Sourdough bakes three Laravel shapes: Laravel + Blade (--laravel), Laravel + Blade + Vue islands (--laravel --vue) and Laravel + Inertia/Vue (--inertia). Each comes with SESAME (sign-in), HELMET (security headers and the /up check), Pinstripe (coding standard), PROCTOR (checks), the Preflight CI components and Squire's deploy files already in it.

Read first:
- https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Sourdough's pages, each one as Markdown; llms-full.txt beside it holds the README too. Fetch what you need; do not work from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: get_project_status and read_project_docs for sourdough answer from the stack's own docs, and policy_lookup gives today's PHP support from CREED. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Check that PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer are on the PATH, and say which versions you found.
2. Install the starter with `composer global require waynestate/sourdough`. If the sourdough command is then not found, add the folder that `composer global config bin-dir --absolute` prints to the PATH.
3. Ask me which shape I want: Blade (`--laravel`), Blade with Vue islands (`--laravel --vue`) or Inertia/Vue (`--inertia`), and whether I want `--sail` or `--docker` for the local runtime. Then bake the app with `sourdough new my-app` and those flags, using the folder name I give you in place of my-app, and change into it.
4. Run `composer install`, then `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate` and `php artisan migrate`. For the islands and Inertia shapes, run `npm install` and `npm run build` before serving. With `--sail` or `--docker` the bake prints the oven's own Next steps; follow those when they differ.
5. Wire in ADVISOR with `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write`, then serve the app with `php artisan serve`, and tell me to open http://localhost:8000. Locally SESAME signs in with its fake driver.
6. Run `sourdough manifest --check` in the app and report what it says.

Constraints:
- The app requires waynestate/playbook, WSU's private shared-values package on git.wayne.edu; the settings in .env.example come from it. If the bake refuses because this machine cannot read the package, tell me; do not pass --no-playbook, which is for CI and automated tests only.
- .sourdough/manifest.json records every file Sourdough wrote. Managed files are Sourdough's; .env.example and README.md are seeded and mine. Commit the manifest.
- The deploy files (build.sh, scripts/release.sh, the .squire/ config) come from Squire. Never edit them by hand.
- Never commit .env, and never paste a secret into a prompt or a file.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess: a folder name, a shape or an oven I have not named, or anything that touches a deploy.

Output: what you ran and what it said, the app's files one level deep, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home. The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

The rest of the bakery
