## Agent ready[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#agent-ready)

The front page is written for people and for the coding agents they use. Every page of this site answers a client that asks for `text/markdown` with the same page as Markdown, and nothing on it phones home: the buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

![The Sourdough front page: the whole recipe card with the two install commands, the Start baking and See the five loaves buttons, and the For your agent row with links to the prompts, the Markdown twin, llms.txt and ChatGPT](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready/hero-menu-1440.png)

### The agent's reading list[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#the-agent-s-reading-list)

- [llms.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists every page of the site with its title and description, points at the prompts and the source, and names the stack's other agent entry points.
- [llms-full.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds the README and every page in one Markdown file.
- Each page has a Markdown twin beside it (`index.md` next to `index.html`), linked from the page head with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`.

An agent that fetches `llms.txt` gets a map; it then fetches only the pages it needs and works from them instead of from memory.

### Recipes for your agent[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#recipes-for-your-agent)

The front page carries three prompts under [Recipes for your agent](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/index.html#agents), ready for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI or ChatGPT. Each tells the agent what Sourdough put in the app and what it must leave alone, and each tells it to ask before it guesses.

![The Recipes for your agent section: three recipe cards, Get started with Sourdough, Check what has drifted in a Sourdough app and Bake a Laravel app with Sourdough, each with its prompt text, a Copy prompt button and Run it in buttons for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI and ChatGPT](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready/agents-1440.png)

#### Recipe No. 1: Get started with Sourdough[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#recipe-no-1-get-started-with-sourdough)

Installs Sourdough, bakes a raw PHP app, fetches WayneUI's standalone file, serves it locally and runs the manifest check. The prompt points the agent at `llms.txt` first, then walks it through `composer global require waynestate/sourdough`, `sourdough new my-app --raw`, the WayneUI fetch, `composer install`, ADVISOR wiring, `php -S localhost:8000 -t public` and `sourdough manifest --check`.

#### Recipe No. 2: Check what has drifted in a Sourdough app[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#recipe-no-2-check-what-has-drifted-in-a-sourdough-app)

Runs `sourdough manifest --check` in an app Sourdough baked, lists the managed files that changed since Sourdough wrote them, and proposes what to put back. It changes nothing, and seeded files never count as drift.

#### Recipe No. 3: Bake a Laravel app with Sourdough[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready.html#recipe-no-3-bake-a-laravel-app-with-sourdough)

Installs Sourdough, bakes one of the three Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue islands or Inertia/Vue) with the oven the developer chooses, serves it locally and runs the manifest check. The prompt points the agent at `llms.txt` first, then walks it through `composer global require waynestate/sourdough`, `sourdough new my-app` with the shape and oven flags, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `npm install` and `npm run build` for the Vue shapes, ADVISOR wiring, `php artisan serve` and `sourdough manifest --check`.

![Recipe No. 1 with the OpenCode button chosen: the prompt rendered as a PowerShell command beside a bash or zsh tab, with a Copy command button](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/agent-ready/prompt-run-opencode-1440.png)

Copy a prompt from the front page, or open it straight in your tool of choice. The commands in a prompt must stay the commands in these docs: the agent-ready check fails a prompt that runs a command the docs do not.

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html

## Changelog[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changelog)

All notable changes to Sourdough are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog; the project follows Semantic Versioning once 1.0 is out.

### Unreleased[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Added: the `sourdough adopt` command, so `sourdough feed` can look after an app Sourdough did not make: `sourdough adopt [<dir>] --shape <shape> [--name <name>] [--sail | --docker] [--no-playbook] [--no-advisor] [--dry-run] [--json] [-v]`. It writes `.sourdough/manifest.json` and nothing else, and prints each template path as `yours`, `seeded` or `missing` (`match` too with `-v`); a top-level folder whose every file is missing prints as one line, and `--json` lists every path. `--shape` is required (the refusal names the shape the app looks like), and the name defaults to the folder's. It refuses, with exit 1, an existing manifest, a leftover `.sourdough/base/`, a name the template cannot use, a folder outside git and a dirty tree; no git, a folder it cannot write and a failed bake are exit 2. A dry run writes nothing and turns the git and writable checks into notes. The wrong-name note now comes at two hinted files, not three, so a raw or laravel-blade app gets it too. Feed's "no manifest" message now says `sourdough adopt <dir> --shape <shape>`. New `tests/AdoptCommandTest.php`, `tests/AdoptFeedTest.php` and the fixture `tests/fixtures/adopt/legacy-raw/`.
- Added: the adopt engine's edge cases, still with no command. A template path that is a symlink, or sits under a symlinked folder, is `yours` ("a symlink: Sourdough never writes through links") even when the link points nowhere, and so is a file whose `realpath()` leaves the app (a Windows junction). A file named in another case (`readme.md` for `README.md` on a case-insensitive disk) is `yours`, named as the disk has it. A file more than twice the template's size plus 1 KiB is `yours` without being read. A `yours` file that lacks the name the template writes into it says so, and two of those add a note that the `--name` may be wrong. The plan's notes also carry the deprecated-shape notice and a note when `.squire.json` records an older or newer Squire kit than the one Sourdough bakes. Adopt refuses a `.sourdough/base/` left from a manifest that is gone. New `tests/AdoptEdgeCasesTest.php`.
- Added: the engine behind the coming `sourdough adopt` (`src/Adopt/`), with no command yet. Given an existing app, a shape and a name, it bakes that shape into a scratch dir through the same Baker `new` and `feed` use, then looks at each template path in the app, and only those: no file is `missing` (left out of the manifest, so the next feed adds it), a file the template seeds is `seeded`, a file equal to the template's (line endings aside) is `match` and recorded as managed, and anything else is `yours`. Every recorded hash is the template's, the answers are the ones `new` would record plus `adopted: true`, and applying writes `.sourdough/manifest.json` and nothing else. It refuses an app that already has a manifest. `Permutation::flags()` now gives the flags a shape implies, for `new --plan` and adopt alike. New `tests/AdoptTest.php`: a lost manifest on every shape and oven adopts back to the bake's record, an edited app keeps its edits and its own files, a CRLF checkout matches, and feed then treats each status as the spec says.
- Added: the manifest has a third file class, `yours`, for the coming `sourdough adopt`: a template file an adopted app keeps its own version of. `sourdough feed` never writes, merges, removes or reports a yours file and keeps no base copy of it, so the generated `sourdough-feed` job stays green; once the app's copy equals the template's, feed records it and manages it from then on. `sourdough manifest --check` skips yours files, as it skips seeded ones. Nothing writes the class yet, and `schema` stays 1. New `tests/FeedYoursClassTest.php`.
- Changed: the deploy kit is Squire 0.10.0 (was 0.9.0): no kit file changed, so the record moves to 0.10.0, and the dev dependency on waynestate/squire is now ^0.10 (locked 0.10.0). The README, the templates reference and the docs index name the 0.10.0 kit too.
- Docs: the README, docs pages and front page catch up with main. Preflight 0.4.0 replaces 0.3.1 and 0.3.0 in the CI guide, MAINTAINING, troubleshooting (the 0.4.0 SHA), BEST_PRACTICES and the vendored a11y checker line; the templates reference names Squire 0.9.0's kit (`^0.9`) and SESAME `^0.6`; the front-end pages show the runtime-only `npm audit --omit=dev`; the CI guide names the Laravel shapes' `proctor-root` job; "in 0.1" claims are gone, and `--describe` is said to stop at the plan. The README says Sourdough starts every shape and that the Laravel shapes keep `oci8` ready. The front page no longer says the generated CI skips `sourdough manifest --check`, lists `package-lock.json` as seeded, adds CREED and ADVISOR to the recipe card and the CI gates to the proofing log, names the release that first baked each loaf, and its footer links the docs and git.wayne.edu. `site/llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` are titled Sourdough again (they said `# .`): the README's title moves out of the centered HTML block the agent-ready kit drops.
- Changed: the Laravel shapes' SESAME config defaults the CAS protocol to 2.0, as SESAME does, because WSU's CAS is believed to refuse the cookieless /p3/ validation CAS 3.0 uses; set SESAME_CAS_PROTOCOL=3.0 for a CAS server that answers it.
- Changed: BEST_PRACTICES.md closes backlog 6, now that PROCTOR has all four checks it asked for: 4.6 is `Checked` on PROCTOR main (`vite-secrets` warns on secret-looking `VITE_` names, not released yet), 4.4 names `app-key` and `env-outside-config` for a committed `.env` and `env()` outside config, and 5.2 names 0.9.0's `case-clash`. Baked apps get `vite-secrets` and `case-clash` once the shapes move past PROCTOR `^0.8`.
- Changed: every shape bakes Squire 0.9.0 (was 0.8.0; the dev dependency is `^0.9`), and the front page's deploy layer moves from kit 0.7.1 to 0.9.0, gaining the portable image files. A Laravel release now stops before anything installs when `APP_KEY` is unset or `APP_DEBUG` is true in production and warns when `APP_ENV` is not production (BEST_PRACTICES 4.14, `Checked` for the release half; every Laravel shape's generator test pins it), and the release gate grades the PHP that runs it (`SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME`).
- Changed: the Vue shapes' npm audit blocks on high or critical advisories in runtime dependencies only (--omit=dev); a second run lists dev-only findings without failing.
- Added: deprecations fail the tests, in Sourdough's own suite and in every shape it bakes (BEST_PRACTICES 4.13, now `Enforced` for the suites). The phpunit config sets `failOnDeprecation` and `failOnPhpunitDeprecation` and skips indirect deprecations; the Laravel shapes get it on the skeleton's `phpunit.xml` at bake time, plus `tests/Support/ReportsDeprecationsToPhpUnit.php`, because Laravel's error handler drops deprecations while testing. Template code bakes clean on PHP 8.5, and the one PHPUnit deprecation in Sourdough's own tests (a doc-comment data provider) is now an attribute.
- Added: the front-end shapes (raw + Vue, Blade + Vue, Inertia) ship a `package-lock.json`, seeded so npm owns it after the bake, and their `frontend` job installs it with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then fails on a high or critical `npm audit` finding (BEST_PRACTICES 4.10, now `Enforced`). New `tests/TemplateNpmLockTest.php` keeps each lock in step with its `package.json`, the smoke jobs install with `npm ci`, and apps already baked get the template's lock from `sourdough feed` only when they have none.
- Added: the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue, Inertia) ship `tests/Feature/JobLimitsTest.php`, which fails on any queued job under `app/Jobs` without Laravel's `#[Tries]` and `#[Timeout]` (the older `$tries` and `$timeout` properties count too) or with a timeout at or above the queue connection's `retry_after`; it passes while there are no jobs and is tested on fixture jobs that break each rule (WELD W18, W20). `stubs/job.queued.stub` and `stubs/job.batched.queued.stub` make `php artisan make:job` write `#[Tries(3)]` and `#[Timeout(45)]`, and `tests/LaravelJobLimitsTest.php` holds every Laravel shape to both.
- Changed: in the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue, Inertia), `/ready` checks the database and the cache as well as the scheduler heartbeat (`app/Health/DatabaseReady.php`, `app/Health/CacheReady.php`), and answers 503 when one fails while `/up` stays liveness and never asks (WELD W11). The route moves from `routes/web.php` to `bootstrap/app.php`, outside the web group, as HELMET's readiness guide asks, so a probe no longer writes a session row or sets a cookie. `tests/Feature/ReadyChecksTest.php` breaks each dependency in turn, and `tests/LaravelReadyChecksTest.php` holds every Laravel shape to it.
- Added: tests/KitRoutesAbsentTest.php: no Laravel shape ships Fortify, Breeze or Jetstream, a routes/auth.php, or registration, password reset, email verification or two-factor routes (BEST_PRACTICES 2.2, backlog 5).
- Added: the generated README carries a Support section with the support line `sourdough new` prints (status, owner and the end-of-security date from CREED's policy), on every shape (BEST_PRACTICES 2.4).
- Changed: the front-end templates floor Vite at ^6.4.1, the CVE-2025-62522 fix line, and ignore \*.local, where Vite keeps local secrets (BEST_PRACTICES 4.12).
- Changed: every app shape and Sourdough's own CI pin Preflight 0.4.0 (87d9b6f; the proctor job clones the full history, so the override-approver check can read git blame).
- Added: WORKER_HEARTBEAT_MAX_AGE=0 turns the scheduler heartbeat check off, so an app that runs no scheduler still answers 200 on /ready.
- Added: new bakes take the PHP floor from CREED's `policy.json` (BEST_PRACTICES 4.2, now `Enforced`). Sourdough requires `waynestate/creed` `^0.1` and reads its policy, or the file `SOURDOUGH_POLICY` names. As of the policy's `refreshed_on`, the floor is the oldest PHP line still supported 365 days later, bounded by the Laravel major's PHP range on the Laravel shapes. It is written into `composer.json` (`require.php`, `config.platform.php`), the `.gitlab-ci.yml` matrix and the README on all five shapes. A policy that cannot be read bakes on the pinned fallback (`^8.3`, tested on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5) and says so. Today's output is unchanged. `sourdough new` prints a `PHP:` line, and `--dry-run --json` gains a `php` object. `tests/PhpFloorTest.php` changes the policy's floor and checks every shape.
- Added: every shape has an owner role, a support status and a sunset path (BEST_PRACTICES 3.7, now `Checked`). The new "Support and sunset" guide (`docs/guides/support.md`) is the policy (the window lengths are a proposal), and `resources/shapes.json` holds the fields. `sourdough new` prints a `Support:` line with the framework's end of security from CREED, and `--dry-run --json` gains `support`. A deprecated shape prints a notice on every `new` and `feed`, and feeding a removed shape names its replacement. `tests/ShapeSupportTest.php` holds the catalog to the rules.
- Changed: the Laravel shapes' `config/helmet.php` holds only the app's `policy_path` override, and HELMET's provider merges the rest from the package (BEST_PRACTICES 3.6). The old 403-line copy had fallen behind HELMET: it had no Playbook lookup for `HELMET_PRESET`, and no `session.secure`, metrics storage or warn settings. Feed replaces an unchanged copy, and an edited one gets a conflict to keep your own keys. 3.6 lists the template code still waiting for a library, starting with `config/sesame.php`, which skips Playbook's CAS URL and defaults CAS to protocol 3.0.
- Added: every shape's pipeline carries three gates from Preflight 0.3.1 (BEST_PRACTICES 4.15, 6.4 and 6.5, now `Enforced`; 3 practices remain `Not yet`). Accessibility: an `a11y-pages` job boots the app with SESAME's fake driver and saves its pages (`/`, plus `/dashboard` signed in on the Laravel shapes), and the `a11y` component checks them at WCAG 2.2 AA, blocking. Bill of materials: the `sbom` component keeps `sbom.cdx.json`, and the front-end shapes' `frontend` job adds `sbom-npm.cdx.json` from CycloneDX's npm tool. Secrets: the `secret-detection` component runs Gitleaks, and a hidden `.deploy` template keeps any future deploy job off merge requests and on protected refs. Each generated README's new "Pipeline" section lists the GitLab settings a file cannot hold. New `tests/TemplateCiGatesTest.php`, plus `testBakedPipelineCarriesTheCiGates` in every generator test, holds all five shapes to it.
- Added: the Laravel + Blade + Vue islands shape has its own `.gitlab-ci.yml` with a `frontend` job (it used to inherit the Blade pipeline, which never built its front end).
- Added: the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue, Inertia) ship Laravel Boost ^2.10 in require-dev, the stack's guidelines in `.ai/guidelines/wayne-state.md` (managed) and starter rules in `.ai/rules/` (seeded), a `.gitignore` block for what `boost:install` writes (`/.mcp.json`, `/boost.json`, `/AGENTS.md`, `/CLAUDE.md`, `/.claude/skills/`, `/.junie/`; `.agents/` stays tracked for Booster), a guarded `composer boost-update` appended to Laravel's `post-update-cmd`, a README section, and `tests/Feature/BoostDevOnlyTest.php`, which fails when Boost leaves require-dev or packages-dev. `tests/BoostWiringTest.php` holds the wiring; BEST_PRACTICES 2.3 is `Enforced`.
- Changed: a Laravel bake drops the skeleton's `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` when they hold only Laravel's Boost bootstrap block (`boost:install` writes them again); a file with other guidance is kept and stays in git. The overlay merge appends `pre-` and `post-` Composer hooks to the skeleton's instead of replacing them, and a new `gitignore-additions.txt` control file adds ignore lines once.
- Changed: `--no-advisor` removes only ADVISOR's own `.mcp.json` line; the Laravel shapes keep `/.mcp.json` ignored for Boost.
- Changed: BEST_PRACTICES.md marks 18 practices with their true status on main (exit codes, output, kit features off, Boost, the Laravel window, MySQL 5.6, env config, VITE\_ secrets, Composer in CI, npm ci, Vite on localhost, the PHP matrix, APP_KEY, CRLF, Docker images, three OSes, templates as archives, boring startup); 9 remain Not yet.
- Added: every app with a front end ships an `.npmrc` with a one-day npm cooldown (`min-release-age=1`), a `.nvmrc` and `engines.node >=22` in its `package.json`; the shapes without a front end get none of it (BEST_PRACTICES 4.9 and 4.11 are `Checked` by the generator tests).
- Changed: every image in the baked CI files is pinned by digest: composer:2.10.3 now carries its multi-arch list digest, like the Node image already did.

#### Added[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added)

- Added: the Laravel shapes schedule a heartbeat each minute and register HELMET's readiness route at /ready with a scheduler check; while the cache stamp is missing or older than WORKER_HEARTBEAT_MAX_AGE seconds (default 180) /ready answers 503, so a stopped scheduler shows up instead of quietly dropping jobs. /up stays the liveness answer and never looks at the cache (WELD W23).
- Changed: the smoke jobs download Composer 2.10.3 and Node 22.23.4 once into a CI cache, check each sha256, and reuse them, instead of fetching both from the internet in every job (D-072).
- Changed: the deploy layer and the templates/squire copy run Squire's kit 0.7.1 (was 0.7.0): .squire/php.ini no longer sets the deprecated session.sid\_\* lines.
- Fixed: the manifest leaves out database/database.sqlite, so sourdough feed never treats an app's database as a template file and WELD's regen gate does not see it as drift.
- Fixed: Laravel bakes (blade, blade-vue, inertia) create an empty database/database.sqlite when .env.example uses sqlite, as Laravel's own installer does, so the printed php artisan migrate runs without a prompt.
- Changed: the scheduled queue worker in the Laravel shapes sets --timeout=45, below the connection's retry_after (Laravel's default 90), and QueueWorkerScheduleTest checks the two (WELD W20).
- Changed: every shape bakes Squire 0.8.0 (was 0.7.1): generated apps get the portable image (`.squire/portable.Dockerfile` and `.squire/portable/`), one image that runs as web, worker, scheduler or migrate for OpenShift, Coolify and raw Docker, and the READMEs say how to build it.
- Added: the Laravel shapes can run the queue from the scheduler, for Citadel where nothing supervises a worker: with QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=scheduler (the new .env.example default) routes/console.php starts queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --tries=3 every minute with withoutOverlapping(10); QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=none leaves the queue to a supervisor. QueueWorkerScheduleTest covers both (WELD W19).
- Changed: the local a11y scripts run Preflight's own checker (vendored from 0.3.1 and pinned by a test), so they check what CI checks: axe-core 4.14.0, 320 and 1280 px, and the reflow check.
- Added: the two Laravel shapes ship tests/Feature/SchedulerNamingTest.php, which fails on any scheduled closure without ->name() (WELD W21).
- CI runs Preflight's a11y component (0.3.1) on site/, every page in light and dark at 320 and 1280 px with the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow check, blocking.
- Changed: every app shape and Sourdough's own CI pin Preflight 0.3.1 (b90323b; fixed cache keys, and caches saved even when a job fails; D-072).
- Added: the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue, Inertia) test that a POST without a CSRF token gets 419, and that a matching token or a same-origin request passes (CsrfTest, WELD W27).
- Changed: every app shape's CI saves its Composer and npm caches even when a job fails, so a retry after a dropped download fetches only what is missing (D-072).
- Fixed: the Laravel shapes' ProductionDebugTest passes the app's own Pint check and every case asserts something.
- Added: Laravel apps (Blade, Blade with Vue, Inertia) refuse to boot in production with APP_DEBUG on (ProductionDebug, beside the dummy-key guard).
- Fixed: the docs menu closes with Escape and hands focus back to its button (docs kit synced from Squire).
- Added: every shape's `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs a `sourdough-feed` job (BEST_PRACTICES 3.2, now `Checked`): on the shape's `composer` image, through `${IMAGE_PREFIX}` and the Composer cache, it installs the newest Sourdough release and runs `sourdough manifest --check` and `sourdough feed --dry-run`. Drift in managed files is listed and never fails (feed merges it); a template release the app has not fed exits 1, which `allow_failure: exit_codes: [1]` shows as a warning, so it never blocks a deploy; exit 2 (no manifest, a newer manifest, leftover conflict markers, a failed bake) fails the job. Apps already baked get the job with their next `sourdough feed`. New `tests/TemplateFeedJobTest.php` holds every shape to the same job and runs its lines on fresh, edited, older and broken bakes of all five shapes and both ovens. BEST_PRACTICES 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 are `Enforced` and name the tests that hold them.

#### Changed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed)

- Changed: new bakes require SESAME ^0.6 (was ^0.5); SESAME 0.6.0 has no breaking change for an app that keeps its driver.
- Docs: the CI guide, MAINTAINING and BEST_PRACTICES name Preflight 0.3.1 (the release the templates pin), and the --no-input help no longer names Sourdough 0.1.
- Changed: new bakes start on the Squire 0.7.0 deploy kit: the release script restarts queue workers and the scheduler after optimize (report only; SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0 turns it off), and the image drops shell functions from the web's PHP (SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS), turns on production opcache (SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE) and reads secrets from /run/secrets. Sourdough's own deploy layer moves too.
- Changed: every app shape's CI caches Composer and npm downloads under a fixed key, so a lock change downloads only what changed.
- Changed: HELMET moves to `^1.0`, its first stable release, wherever this repo requires it.
- Changed: every shape requires PROCTOR ^0.8 (was ^0.7): the raw `composer.json` and both Laravel overlays. Breaking for apps you feed whose deploy scripts have Windows line endings, which PROCTOR 0.8's `crlf-deploy-script` fails; the upgrading page has the steps. The deploy layer requires PROCTOR ^0.8 (locked 0.8.0).

#### Fixed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed)

- Fixed: scripts/a11y.ps1 works on a Windows checkout with CRLF line endings; it strips the carriage returns from the shell command it hands to Docker, which sh rejected with a syntax error.
- Fixed: the docs kit's copy button no longer covers the first line of code when it says Copied or Failed: over the code it keeps its resting width and shows a check or a cross when the word does not fit (docs kit synced from Squire).
- Fixed: `sourdough manifest --check` forgives line endings, as `sourdough feed` does. The raw shapes' `.gitattributes` checks `*.ps1` out with CRLF, so every clone of a fresh raw app reported `scripts/parity.ps1` as changed. `tests/ManifestCommandTest.php` covers it.
- Fixed: BEST_PRACTICES.md practice 3.4 counts the 0.2.0 tag among the releases that follow the release steps.

### 0.2.0 (2026-11-08)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-0-2026-11-08)

#### Added[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-1)

- Added: `tests/PreflightPinTest.php`: one Preflight version across every shape's pipeline and Sourdough's own GitLab pipeline; no component `image` input with a registry prefix; every Docker Hub component in a shape takes the shape's `IMAGE_PREFIX`. BEST_PRACTICES 4.3 is `Enforced` by it. `tests/TemplateCiCacheTest.php` now checks the `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/` rule on the app's own jobs only.
- Added: a third agent recipe on the front page, for the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade with Vue islands and Inertia/Vue), and the stale "join the rack" line is gone.
- Added: every bake saves its plan in the app as `.sourdough/plan.yaml` (ADR-0014, decision 3), after the bake succeeds: a `--plan` bake saves that plan with the name the app got, a bake from flags saves the shape, the name and all four parts. The file is not in the manifest, so it is neither managed nor seeded: `sourdough feed` and `sourdough manifest --check` never read, rewrite or flag it, and feed writes none for apps baked before. `--plan` now reads YAML plans (`.yaml` or `.yml`) as well as JSON, through the same schema, so the saved plan bakes the same loaf again. Sourdough requires `symfony/yaml` `^7.4`. `tests/SavedPlanTest.php` and `tests/FeedCommandTest.php` cover it.

#### Changed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-1)

- Changed: every shape's `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins the Preflight CI components to the 0.3.0 release SHA (`23038dfe767f6ef60e3b2efca1128f53d9acdff7` with `# 0.3.0`, was 0.1.4; Preflight 0.2.0 and later need GitLab 18.7 or later). From Preflight 0.3.0 each Docker Hub component adds the registry prefix itself (`image_prefix`, D-054), so the includes pass `image_prefix: "${IMAGE_PREFIX}"` and drop their `image` inputs, which only carried the prefix in front of the components' own defaults: the components and the app's own jobs follow one proxy rule. Apps already baked take it with `sourdough feed`; a Preflight include an owner added with a prefixed `image` keeps the plain name (docs/upgrading.md).
- Changed: Sourdough's own GitLab pipeline pins the Preflight components to the `0.3.0` release tag (was 0.1.4), and their `image` inputs are plain names (the components add the proxy prefix); the jobs Sourdough defines itself keep `${CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX}/`. The GitHub workflow stays on Preflight 0.1.4: GitHub's copy of Preflight has no tag after 0.1.4 yet (D-069).
- Changed: the `--docker` setup publishes its ports on 127.0.0.1 only, so the dev server and Vite are not reachable from the network (SOURDOUGH-25).
- The front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) runs Squire's kit 0.6.0 (was 0.5.0): `scripts/release.sh` asks PROCTOR's deploy gate for a go or no-go on each release (a report, not a stop, unless `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), and `.env.squire.example` lists the new setting. The layer's pins move to HELMET `^0.4` (locked 0.4.0) and PROCTOR `^0.7` (locked 0.7.0).
- Docs: the Docker commands in the README and docs mount the shared `stack-composer-cache` volume, so Composer downloads are cached between runs.
- Changed: apps start on the Squire 0.6.0 deploy kit (was 0.4.0). The copy in `templates/squire/` comes from Squire 0.6.0, and the dev dependency is `^0.6`.
- Changed: a baked app's `scripts/release.sh` asks PROCTOR's deploy gate (`proctor gate`) for a go or no-go instead of running `proctor check`, right after `composer audit` and before the frontend build and the migrations, so `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce` stops a no-go before it touches the database. The verdict goes to `storage/squire/proctor-gate.json` (new setting `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_RECORD_DIR`, listed in `.env.squire.example`; the folder ignores itself) and becomes the baseline the next release is ratcheted against, so a failure that is already live is held and only a new one blocks. With a PROCTOR that has no `gate` the step warns and runs `proctor check` as before.
- Changed: new apps in every shape require HELMET `^0.4` (was `^0.3`), SESAME `^0.5` (was `^0.4`) and PROCTOR `^0.7` (was `^0.6`); CREED stays `^0.1` (0.1.7 today). PROCTOR 0.7 brings `proctor gate`, which the kit's release script now asks; HELMET 0.4's request metrics stay off until `HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE` is set. `tests/StackPinsTest.php` checks all three in every template composer file.
- Changed: the Laravel shapes' `config/sesame.php` names SESAME 0.5's `cas.require_pending_login` (env `SESAME_CAS_REQUIRE_PENDING_LOGIN`, default on), with a note to leave it on; the Laravel adapter already hands the cas driver the session.
- Changed: every shape's `.gitlab-ci.yml` caches its downloads. Docker Hub images in the app's own jobs are `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/<image>`, digest pins kept, and the Preflight components get the same prefix as their `image_prefix` input; `IMAGE_PREFIX` defaults to `docker.io`, and a `workflow:` rule sets it to the group's GitLab Dependency Proxy when the GitLab has one. Composer and npm installs extend `.composer-cache` (keyed on `composer.lock`) and `.npm-cache` (keyed on `package-lock.json` and `package.json`). A project variable `IMAGE_PREFIX=docker.io` skips the proxy. New `tests/TemplateCiCacheTest.php` keeps every shape that way. Apps already baked take it with `sourdough feed`.

#### Fixed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed-1)

- Fixed: the pipeline's PROCTOR jobs no longer pass `--policy`, which PROCTOR 0.7 refuses in CI; PROCTOR checks against the CREED policy it bundles.
- Fixed: BEST_PRACTICES.md's "Keeping generated apps current" tags match the code, each naming the file that holds it: 3.1 (record where the app came from) and 3.3 (merge, not overwrite) are `Enforced` by the manifest and `sourdough feed`, 3.2 (a check that fails CI) is `Partly enforced` (`feed --dry-run` and `manifest --check` exist; no template runs them in CI yet), 3.4 (tags and migration notes) is `Documented` in the release steps, and 3.5 (compatibility CI) is `Checked` by the smoke gate, which still only warns. They all said `Not yet` or `Documented`. 4.3 keeps `Partly enforced` and now names its templates and test.
- Fixed: BEST_PRACTICES.md describes Sourdough as it is (0.1.7, all five shapes bake, `manifest` and `feed` ship) instead of a tool with no code on main, and practice 6.1 (wire the stack in by default) is `Enforced` by the generator tests in every shape; it said only the raw shape generated.
- Fixed: the local parity fallback image builds when the host's uid or gid already belongs to an account in the image (a host gid of 1001, like GitHub's runners, collided with the container user's default).
- Fixed: `scripts/parity.ps1` builds the fallback image with the host's uid and gid (1000 on Windows, the current user's ids on Linux and macOS) instead of a fixed 1000, so the app container starts when the bind-mounted source belongs to another user.
- Fixed: the raw shapes (`--raw`, `--raw --vue`) sign in with CAS in production. `public/index.php` called `DriverFactory::make($config)` with no HTTP client, so with `APP_ENV=production` the cas driver refused to boot; it now passes a Guzzle client (10 second timeout, no redirects, TLS verification on), a `nyholm/psr7` request factory and the app's `NativeSession`, which SESAME 0.5's cas driver needs for its pending-login marker (a ticket is accepted only for a sign-in this browser started). The raw template requires `guzzlehttp/guzzle` `^7.9 || ^8.0` and `nyholm/psr7` `^1.8`.

### 0.1.7 (2026-11-07)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-7-2026-11-07)

#### Added[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-2)

- Added: `sourdough feed` brings template updates into an app made with `sourdough new`, without clobbering what the app changed (ADR-0014, decision 4). It bakes the app's shape again with the answers in its manifest and goes file by file: files the template did not change are left alone, untouched managed files take the new version, files both sides changed are three-way merged by `git merge-file`, same-line changes get git's conflict markers (`<<<<<<< app` ... `>>>>>>> sourdough <version>`) and never a silent overwrite, new template files are added, dropped ones are removed only when untouched, binary files are never merged (the template's copy lands as `<file>.sourdough-new`), and seeded files are never touched. The base for a merge is found by its manifest hash, in `.sourdough/base/` (the template's version of each changed managed file, kept by the previous feed) or anywhere in the app's git history; with no base, both versions are marked. Feed then moves the manifest to the new base. It runs only on a clean git tree, refuses while the last feed's markers are unresolved, and refuses a manifest from a newer Sourdough. `--dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing (exit `0` fresh, `1` feeding would change files, so it works as a CI gate), `--json` prints the plan for machines; a real feed exits `0` fed cleanly, `1` fed with conflicts, `2` tool error. It needs git and nothing else. Every shape is covered by `tests/FeedCommandTest.php`, and the smoke gate now checks that a fresh bake of each shape has nothing to feed.
- Added: the proof harness, `scripts/proof.sh` (Linux, macOS) and `scripts/proof.ps1` (Windows), and the Proof page (`docs/reference/proof.md`) with its dated Last run table. In Docker, one after another, it runs the smoke gate on all five shapes and on every Laravel shape with `--sail` and with `--docker` (eleven runs), and feeds a bake of the last release (read from this changelog) forward in each. It writes `proof-out/last-run.md`, a summary and every step log, and exits `1` when any run fails. A GitLab `proof` job runs it by hand or on a schedule that sets `SOURDOUGH_PROOF` to `1`, never on a push, and keeps the results as an artifact. `tests/ProofHarnessTest.php` keeps the two scripts, the gate, the CI job and the table listing the same runs.
- Added: the smoke gate checks more of every loaf. Right after the bake, `sourdough manifest --check` must be clean. Every shape runs its own suite as its own step (the count goes in the proof table) and `composer proctor`. The Laravel shapes now boot too, on Laravel's own router: `/` must answer with the shape's home page (the Blade page, the built Vue islands, or the Inertia `Home` page), `/dashboard` after SESAME's fake sign-in, `/nope` 404 and `/up` 200; the raw shape's `/` must carry its home page in WayneUI's shell. A second argument, `--sail` or `--docker`, proves a Laravel shape's oven (the scaffold's files, install, suite, PROCTOR), and `SMOKE_FEED_FROM=<version>` bakes that release from Packagist and feeds it forward. `scripts/smoke-shape.ps1` takes `-Oven` and `-FeedFrom` to match.
- Added: the Laravel shapes ship skeleton feature tests (`tests/Feature/SkeletonTest.php`, Pest, next to the starter's example tests): `/up` answers 200, the home page answers 200 for a guest (the Blade page, the built Vue island, or the Inertia `Home` component), a guest at `/dashboard` goes to the sign-in flow, the dashboard renders for a signed-in user after SESAME's fake sign-in (with the islands view's `data-vue-island="counter"` island and the Inertia `Dashboard` component checked too), a missing page answers 404, and `UserResolver::refreshUser()` turns a stored user array back into the `User` by username, or `null` when the username no longer exists. Each baked Laravel suite grows from two tests to nine, and the proof table quotes the new counts.

#### Changed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-2)

- Changed: the front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) runs Squire's kit 0.5.0 (was 0.4.0): `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` and `scripts/parity.ps1` take the new templates, so `squire init --check` passes. `site/assets/stack-env.js` takes the stack's one copy, with bindingless catch blocks.
- Changed: The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.
- Changed: the Inertia shape bakes on Inertia 3: `inertiajs/inertia-laravel` `^3.0` and `@inertiajs/vue3` `^3.0` (PHP 8.2+, Laravel 11+, ESM only, no bundled Axios). The root view marks its title `data-inertia` instead of the bare `inertia` attribute, and Inertia now hands the first page to Vue in a `<script type="application/json">` element instead of the root div's `data-page` attribute (HELMET's CSP is untouched: a JSON data block never runs). The template never used Axios, `Inertia::lazy()`, `router.cancel()` or the `future` options, so the rest of it bakes as before (one fix rides along: the progress bar's nonce, below). Apps already baked: the Upgrading page's Unreleased section has the steps (`sourdough feed`, then `composer update` and `npm install`).
- Changed: new apps in every shape require PROCTOR `^0.6` (was `^0.4`). The Laravel shapes' `composer proctor` script is now plain `proctor check`: PROCTOR 0.6 refuses `--policy` in CI unless the job sets `PROCTOR_ALLOW_OVERRIDES=1`, and without the option it still reads CREED's released policy from `vendor/waynestate/creed` on its own. PROCTOR 0.6 also fails `composer-audit` when the app has no `composer.lock` or Composer is not on `PATH`; every baked pipeline installs first, so a baked app passes as before.
- Changed: the smoke gate reads the Inertia `Home` and `Dashboard` pages from Inertia 3's JSON page element, and `tests/StackPinsTest.php` keeps the PROCTOR and Inertia lines, the plain `proctor check` script and the `data-inertia` title from slipping back.

#### Fixed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed-2)

- Fixed: the Inertia shape's progress bar wears its styles again. Inertia injects them in an inline `<style>`, and HELMET's CSP admits one only with the request's nonce, so the browser refused it on every page ("Refused to apply inline style") and the bar ran unstyled. `resources/js/app.ts` now reads the nonce from the pre-paint script's `nonce` property and hands it to Inertia 3's new `nonce` option, which stamps it on everything Inertia injects; no CSP is loosened.
- Fixed: the Laravel templates' `UserResolver` lists its interfaces in Pint's order (`RefreshesUser` before `UserResolverContract`), so a freshly baked app passes its own `pint --test` on the first run instead of failing `composer ci`.
- Fixed: Baked apps pin `config.platform.php` to their PHP floor, so PROCTOR no longer flags the lock.
- Fixed: Baked Laravel apps read the signed-in user again on every request, so Laravel 13's JSON sessions no longer sign everyone out after the first page.
- Fixed: `sourdough feed` brings an app baked by 0.1.6 with `--sail` or `--docker` forward with its oven. 0.1.6 wrote the manifest before the oven's scaffold ran, so the answers named no oven, the oven's files were not in it, and `composer.json` was hashed before the scaffold edited it: feed baked the plain shape, found it "Fresh", and left `sourdough manifest --check` reporting `composer.json` changed for good. Feed now reads the oven from the app's files when a 0.1.6 manifest names none (a `Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml` and the `dev-up` script for Docker; `laravel/sail` and Sail's `compose.yaml` for Sail) and says so in a `note:` line. The proof harness found it.
- Fixed: `sourdough feed` records a managed file that already holds the template's new version (a new `record` action) instead of passing over it in silence. Nothing in the file is written, but the manifest moves to the new hash, so `sourdough manifest --check` stops calling it changed. A plan of only `record` lines is a change: `--dry-run` exits `1`, and the real feed writes the manifest.
- Fixed: a 0.1.6 oven bake feeds forward without a `composer.json` conflict: the manifest hashed the file before the scaffold edited it, so feed undoes the scaffold's edit to recover the pre-scaffold composer data, verifies it against the recorded hash, reapplies the scaffold and uses the result as the merge base; an app that never touched the file takes the template's `composer.json` as an update, and a real app edit still merges or conflicts as before.
- Fixed: the manifest of an app baked with `--sail` or `--docker` lists the scaffold's files (`Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml`, `.dockerignore`, the `docker/` ini files) and the composer.json the scaffold edited, and records `sail` or `docker` in its answers again, so `sourdough manifest --check` is clean right after the bake. It was written before the scaffold ran, so the check reported `composer.json` as changed on a fresh app. `new` and `feed` now bake through one `Baker`.
- Fixed: the front page's feeding schedule shows its rows again for visitors who allow motion. Each row is clipped until it wipes in, and Chromium counts a clipped row as 0 % visible, so the reveal's 20 % threshold never fired and the rows stayed blank. The reveal now trips on the row's first edge, 15 % above the bottom of the screen.
- Fixed: the docs pages reflow at 320 px (WCAG 1.4.10). The version ticket in the shared header carried `flex-shrink: 0`, so the header row could not give up ground and every docs page measured 328 px wide in a 320 px viewport. The ticket now shrinks and wraps to its version number instead of holding its width. The front page's five crumb buttons are named by their visible words too: each `aria-label` starts with "Score it", the words the hint shows, so the accessible name contains the visible text (axe `label-content-name-mismatch`).

### 0.1.6 (2026-11-06)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-6-2026-11-06)

#### Added[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-3)

- Added: the site accessibility gate: `scripts/a11y.sh` (Git Bash, Linux, macOS) and `scripts/a11y.ps1` (Windows) run axe-core (WCAG 2.2 AA) in Docker over every committed HTML page under `site/`, in light and dark at 360 px and 1280 px.
- Added: `sourdough new --raw --vue` bakes a raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON app, the fifth and last shape. The raw template comes first (HELMET, the session and SESAME boot the same way, Squire's deploy files, Pinstripe, PROCTOR, Playbook and ADVISOR wiring), then `templates/raw-vue/` over it: a front controller that answers JSON under `/api/` (`/api/me` returns the signed-in user, or `401` instead of sending a `fetch()` to CAS) and sends the Vue page for `/` (and for any other path, with a `404`); Vue 3 and Vite with WayneUI's Vue components and its layered dist stylesheet from `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` and `@waynestate/wayne-ui-css` 2.0.8, pinned exactly as in the Inertia shape; and `src/Vite.php`, a small tested reader for Vite's manifest that prints the tags with HELMET's CSP nonce, or points at the dev server while `npm run dev` runs (and adds it to the CSP, never in production). Its Next steps: `composer install`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, `composer serve`. The `--raw --vue` plan no longer ends in "not available in this release", and a `smoke-raw-vue` CI job bakes the shape and checks `/`, `/api/me` and `/up` on a live server. All five loaves bake now.
- Added: the Laravel shapes refuse to boot production on the tests' dummy APP_KEY (`app/Support/DummyAppKey.php`, called from `AppServiceProvider::boot()`), and `tests/Support/SkipEnvFile.php` hands the tests that one dummy key (base64 of 32 zero bytes) when nothing else sets one. WELD ships the same files.
- Added: the docs site in `site/docs/` is built by the shared Squire docs-site builder (`bin/docs-site.php`) from the pages in `docs/`, and `composer ci` checks it with `@docs:check`.
- Added: the smoke gate proves a live baked raw app serves: it fetches the pinned WayneUI release once into `public/wayne-ui.php`, starts the app with `APP_ENV=local` on `127.0.0.1:8099` and expects `/` 200, `/nope` 404 and `/up` 200. Every shape now bakes with `--no-playbook`, because Playbook is required by default and its private package cannot be installed credential-free.
- Added: `--docker` generates the app's own Docker setup for the Laravel shapes (`--laravel`, `--laravel --vue` and `--inertia`): a two-target `Dockerfile` (dev and prod) whose base images are pinned by manifest-list digest, so one pin resolves natively on amd64 and arm64, a `compose.yaml` with a MySQL 8.4 service (and a vite service for the Vue and Inertia shapes), a `.dockerignore`, the PHP ini files the image copies in, the `composer dev-up`, `dev-down` and `dev-shell` scripts, the database settings in `.env.example`, and a "Run it locally with Docker" README section. It works natively on Windows, macOS and Linux (no WSL2 needed). Playbook credentials reach a production build only as a BuildKit secret, never a build arg, and the `FROM` lines are the single place to swap in SQUIRE's Citadel-parity image when it exists.
- Added: `--sail` generates a Sail setup (compose.yaml, laravel/sail) for the Laravel shapes.
- Added: the raw template's `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs an explicit `composer-ci` job (`composer install`, then `composer ci`), mirroring the Laravel overlay, so PROCTOR sees a `composer ci` in the pipeline instead of warning that no job runs it.
- Added: generated apps in Require mode get a `composer playbook` script (`@composer show waynestate/playbook --no-interaction`) with its `scripts-descriptions` entry, so you can check any time whether Playbook (WSU shared values) is installed. Existing scripts keep their order and `playbook` is appended last; an existing `playbook` script is left alone.
- Added: the raw template ships Pinstripe's coding standard: `pint.json` (the per preset, with the fetched `public/wayne-ui.php` kept out and `vendor` excluded) and `phpstan.neon` (Pinstripe's raw preset, level 8 over `src/` and `public/`), `waynestate/pinstripe` in require-dev with the extension-installer plugin allowed, and `lint`, `fix` and `analyse` scripts, so `composer ci` runs test, lint, analyse, proctor and audit in that order.
- Added: the front page's main nav links the docs site.

#### Changed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-3)

- Changed: the Inertia shape draws with WayneUI instead of the Tailwind starter kit, the same wiring WELD ships. `@waynestate/wayne-ui-css` and `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` 2.0.8 are pinned exactly; every page wears WayneUI's app bar (shield, theme toggle), the sidebar that becomes a focus-trapping drawer on phones, breadcrumbs, cards and footer; a pre-paint script under HELMET's nonce stops the dark-mode flash; Ziggy's client comes from the `ziggy-js` npm package. The home page and the dashboard are new, in WayneUI's components and tokens. `eslint.config.js` refuses `components/ui` imports and the kit's helper packages, `.prettierrc` is the stack's, and a `frontend` CI job runs lint, Prettier, vue-tsc and the build.
- Changed: the Laravel shapes (Blade, Blade + Vue, Inertia) generate apps on Pest 4 (`tests/Pest.php`, a Pest example test, `composer test` and `composer ci` run Pest, PHPUnit tests unchanged, tests read `.env`, or `.env.example` when there is no `.env`); the raw shape is unchanged.
- Changed: the docs site wears Sourdough's own look: the front page header and menu (Docs marked current), the gold version ticket, Caprasimo titles, the baker's Kalam hand for labels, the recipe terminal with its gold Copy pill for commands, recipe-card tables, baker's-note callouts and the deep green footer, with a derived chalkboard dark mode. Source: `docs/_header.html`, `docs/theme/sourdough.css` and a `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`; the kit's `docs.css` is unchanged.
- Changed: `sourdough new` now requires `waynestate/playbook` in every app it bakes: the VCS repository, the package in `require`, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends the token to git.wayne.edu, the `.env.example` block, and a README section with the access how-to. The command checks read access before writing anything (a Composer credential, then a direct git probe) and refuses with exit `1` until the developer can read the package; an unreachable git.wayne.edu generates with a warning, and non-interactive and CI runs skip the check. `--playbook` stays as a no-op for old scripts, and `--no-playbook` is for CI and automated tests only.
- Changed: the raw template's code passes both of Pinstripe's tools: per-preset style fixes in `Oracle`, `OracleException`, `public/index.php` and `OracleTest`, precise closure and binds types in `Oracle`, a false guard for `oci_error()` results, and the connect-failure branch reporting the last driver error instead of passing the failed connection as its source. A freshly baked raw app passes its own checks.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: CI pins Preflight 0.1.4 (GitLab component includes and the GitHub reusable workflow at its tag commit); the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Changed: new apps now get HELMET `^0.3`, SESAME `^0.4` and PROCTOR `^0.4`, and their `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins the Preflight CI components to the 0.1.4 release SHA (`79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8`, with the tag in a trailing comment) because PROCTOR 0.4's `preflight-pinned` check wants a 40-hex SHA.
- Changed: the smoke gate runs `php artisan migrate` like the Next steps, and the Laravel template READMEs show `migrate` for local and `migrate --force` for deploys.

#### Removed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#removed)

- Removed: from the Inertia shape, `tailwind.config.js`, `cn()` (`resources/js/lib/utils.ts`), `tailwindcss`, `autoprefixer`, `tailwind-merge`, `clsx`, `lucide-vue-next`, `@vueuse/core`, `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`, the Bunny Fonts link and the ten kit components they served.

#### Fixed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed-3)

- Fixed: `--sail` apps answer 200 on `/` and `/up` when the checkout is one Sail's `sail` user cannot write (a Windows drive under Docker Desktop, or files a root container wrote). Every page was a 500 naming `tempnam()`, because Blade could not write `storage/framework/views`. The compose file's entrypoint now gives the `sail` user its `WWWUSER` uid first (so a `sail artisan` run the moment `sail up -d` returns no longer runs as the image's uid 1337 and leaves a log file the server cannot append to), opens the app's files to that user only when it cannot write them (`vendor/`, `node_modules/` and `.git` untouched), then starts Sail as usual.
- Fixed: `--docker` apps with a vite service (Blade + Vue, Inertia) serve `/` on the first `composer dev-up`. Nothing installed `node_modules`, so the vite service exited with `vite: not found` and `/` was a 500 (`Vite manifest not found`). The service now runs `npm install` when Vite is missing, then `npm run dev`.
- Fixed: the Laravel shapes' (Blade, Blade + Vue, Inertia) `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs the php-test matrix with `vendor/bin/pest`. The Preflight component defaults to `vendor/bin/phpunit`, which refuses the Pest example tests ("Please run ./vendor/bin/pest instead"), so every job in the matrix crashed with exit 255. Pest runs the PHPUnit class tests too.
- Fixed: `--docker` apps with a vite service (Blade + Vue, Inertia) load their pages. The service ran `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0`, so laravel-vite-plugin wrote `http://0.0.0.0:5173` to `public/hot` and the browser got a blank page; it now runs `npm run dev` with `LARAVEL_SAIL=1`, which listens on every address and writes `http://localhost:5173`.
- Fixed: the GitLab smoke jobs (raw, Blade, Blade + Vue, Inertia) failed before they started: the Composer installer's options were handed to `php` itself (`no argument for option -`). They now go after `--`, with Composer pinned to 2.10.3, and the image gets `unzip` so Composer can unpack the locked packages.
- Fixed: a freshly baked Laravel app passes its own `pint --test` again: the Pest example tests are written out over several lines and `tests/Support/SkipEnvFile.php` uses imports and Laravel's operator order, so `composer ci` no longer fails on the template's own style.
- Fixed: raw apps start with `composer serve`. The old `php -S localhost:8000 -t public` line booted the app as production, because the raw front controller defaults `APP_ENV` to production when it is unset. The raw template's new `serve` script disables Composer's process timeout, sets `APP_ENV=local` cross-platform with `@putenv`, then starts `php -S localhost:8000 -t public`, so SESAME signs in with its fake driver; the raw Next steps, the raw README and the site recipe all point at `composer serve` now.
- Fixed: the raw front controller answers `404` for any path but `/` (a short not-found page that keeps WayneUI's layout and links home) instead of rendering the home page for every URL. `/up` stays HELMET's and answers first.
- Fixed: the GitHub CI workflow was rejected as invalid (every run failed with "workflow file issue") because the smoke job used GitLab's `allow_failure`; it now uses `continue-on-error`.
- Fixed: the sourdough command now works after composer global require (bin/sourdough also looks for the autoloader three folders up, where a dependency install keeps it).
- Fixed: the Laravel Next steps now run `php artisan migrate` after `php artisan key:generate` (all three Laravel shapes), so a freshly baked app has its database before the first request instead of answering 500 until someone migrates by hand.
- Fixed: the Blade and Blade + Vue islands views read the signed-in user as an array (`$user['name']`), because SESAME's `Sesame::user()` returns an array, not an object; the dashboard and the layout no longer crash after sign-in.
- Fixed: the laravel-blade template ships `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` with `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` like the laravel-inertia one, so string columns stay inside Citadel's MySQL 5.6 index limit (PROCTOR `mysql56-string-default`).
- Fixed: the Oracle check command in the laravel-blade and laravel-inertia templates compares in Pint's non-Yoda order (`$script === null`), so a freshly baked app passes its own `composer ci` on the first run.
- Fixed: the laravel-blade-vue template ships `tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php` with `$this->withoutVite()`, so `composer ci` in a freshly baked islands app no longer fails on the missing Vite manifest before `npm run build` has run.
- Fixed: the Playbook wiring no longer drops a template's own composer config keys.
- Fixed: the raw template ships `stubs/wayne-ui.php`, a static-analysis stub for the run-time WayneUI functions (`wsu_shell_start`, `wsu_shell_end`) that `phpstan.neon` scans through `scanFiles`, so `composer ci` in a freshly baked raw app no longer fails with function-not-found errors for functions that arrive only with the fetched `public/wayne-ui.php`.

#### Security[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#security)

- Security: the front-page deploy layer moves to Symfony 7.4.23 (symfony/http-foundation and symfony/yaml advisories, including CVE-2026-118514).

### 0.1.5 (2026-11-03)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-5-2026-11-03)

#### Added[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-4)

- Added: `sourdough new --laravel` bakes a Laravel + Blade app: a fresh Laravel skeleton from Composer, the laravel-blade overlay, the stack packages, Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest. Its Next steps suit the shape: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan serve`. One more loaf on the bench.
- Added: `sourdough new --inertia` bakes a Laravel + Inertia/Vue app: the same Laravel skeleton, the laravel-inertia overlay (Inertia pages rendered by Vue, Ziggy routes, the stack packages), Squire's laravel deploy files and the manifest. Its Next steps suit the shape: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, `php artisan serve`. Three of the five loaves bake now.
- Added: `sourdough new --laravel --vue` bakes a Laravel + Blade + Vue islands app: the Laravel + Blade bake under a front-end layer (Vite with the Vue plugin, a `resources/js/app.js` registry that mounts a Vue 3 app on every `[data-vue-island]` element, and a Counter island live on the dashboard view). Its Next steps suit the shape: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, `php artisan serve`. Four of the five loaves bake now.
- Added: the raw template ships `scripts` (`test`, `proctor`, `ci`) and `scripts-descriptions`, so a generated raw app can run its own gate locally with `composer ci`.
- Added: generated apps ship ADVISOR by default. `waynestate/advisor` lands in `require-dev` (raw template and the laravel-blade overlay), `.mcp.json` is git-ignored, the README gains an "ADVISOR" section, and the Next steps print `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write`. `--no-advisor` skips all of it and records the choice in the manifest.
- Added: the smoke gate (`scripts/smoke-shape.sh`, `scripts/smoke-shape.ps1`, `scripts/smoke.Dockerfile`) bakes a shape with this checkout's own CLI and runs the generated app's own checks; CI runs one job per shape, all `allow_failure: true` until seen green once.

#### Changed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-4)

- Changed: `--name` on the Laravel bakes reaches every place WELD applies it by hand: `composer.json`'s `name` becomes `app/<slug>` (an application is not a published package) with the description reading ", a Wayne State app baked from Sourdough.", `.env.example`'s `APP_NAME` carries the app name (quoted when it holds a space), and the `config/app.php` default follows it.

- Changed: the Squire copy comes from Squire 0.4.0 (adds oracle-check.php to every target; the dev dependency is now ^0.4).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in ./.env.squire).
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local .env.squire file is now git-ignored).

The Laravel + Blade, Laravel + Blade + Vue islands and Laravel + Inertia/Vue loaves come out of the oven with their real commands; the hero, the rack note and the two agent prompts name the four that bake in 0.1; and WELD reads as the Inertia/Vue shape already built from Sourdough, not the other starter. #### Fixed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed-4)

- Fixed: the laravel-inertia overlay now passes a real run of a generated app. The overlay allows `phpstan/extension-installer` in composer config so `composer install` succeeds, the appended SESAME and HELMET env keys ship commented out (except `SESAME_DRIVER=fake`) so package defaults hold instead of being overridden by empty values, the generator removes the skeleton's `vite.config.js` so it no longer sits next to the overlay's `vite.config.ts` and breaks `npm run build`, and the Oracle command, Oracle error helper and bootstrap are Pint-clean like their Blade twins.

- Fixed: the agent-ready site twins (`site/index.md`, `site/llms-full.txt`) are resynced with the README, so the `site:agent-ready-check` step of `composer ci` passes.
- Fixed: the laravel-inertia template boots a fresh app out of the box: `config/sesame.php` defaults `SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME` to `jane.doe` so the fake driver has a non-empty username, and Pint skips the two verbatim Squire files (`health.php`, `oracle-check.php`) through `notPath`.

## CI[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#ci)

Sourdough's pipelines run one gate, `composer ci`, on both forges: the same command on GitLab and GitHub. This page covers what each pipeline runs, what green means, and where the pipelines should run. For what the gate contains, continue to [Testing](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html).

Tip

Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner.

### On GitLab[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#on-gitlab)

Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5) and `composer-audit` components, plus a `composer-ci` job. The raw shapes add the `proctor` component; the Laravel shapes run PROCTOR in a `proctor-root` job (`composer proctor`, which is `proctor check`). Every shape also includes three gates, `sbom`, `secret-detection` and `a11y`, and ships a `.deploy` template for deploy jobs; they are described below. Every include is pinned to the Preflight 0.4.0 release commit (`87d9b6fc6b0ed302dd729986525282cd7b567ebd`), with the tag in a trailing comment.

### The accessibility gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#the-accessibility-gate)

Every shape's pipeline checks the app's own pages in a real browser (BEST_PRACTICES 6.4). Two jobs share the work, so the checking stays Preflight's:

1. `a11y-pages` boots the app the way its first run on a desk does, with SESAME's fake driver: PHP's built-in server for the raw shapes, `php artisan serve` (after `.env`, a key and an SQLite database) for the Laravel shapes. The shapes with a front end wait for the `frontend` job (`needs: [frontend]`) and serve its build. The job copies `public/`'s static files (never its PHP) into `a11y-site/` and saves each path in `A11Y_PATHS` there as `<path>/index.html`, through one cookie jar, so a page behind sign-in is saved signed in. The server's own origin is cut out of the saved pages, so their links work on any port. `A11Y_DATA` (raw + Vue only: `/api/me`) saves the JSON the page fetches as it loads, so the Vue app draws its signed-in view.
2. Preflight's `a11y` component (`site_dir: a11y-site`, `needs: [a11y-pages]`) opens each page in Chromium with axe-core, light and dark, at 320 and 1280 px, plus the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow check, at WCAG 2.2 AA (WayneUI's floor; the ADA Title II rule names 2.1 AA, which 2.2 AA includes). It blocks: a violation fails the pipeline.

| Shape | `A11Y_PATHS` | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw PHP | `/` | the one page, signed in by the fake driver |
| Raw PHP + Vue SPA | `/` (and `/api/me` in `A11Y_DATA`) | the Vue app with the signed-in user |
| Laravel + Blade, Blade + Vue islands, Inertia | `/ /dashboard` | the home page signed out, then the dashboard after `/login` signs in |

In production the sign-in page is the CAS server's own, so the part of the sign-in flow an app draws is the signed-in page it lands on. An app owner adds each new page to `A11Y_PATHS` and to the a11y include's `pages` (the two lists name the same pages; `tests/TemplateCiGatesTest.php` holds the templates to that). Every shape renders pages, so every shape gets the gate; an app that later becomes a pure JSON API with no pages can drop the `a11y` include and the `a11y-pages` and `a11y` jobs together.

Note

Automated checks find only part of the problems. axe-core checks a loaded page; it does not follow a client-side navigation, so focus after a route change and announced route changes in the Vue shapes still need a person with a keyboard and a screen reader. The generated README says so.

### The npm install and audit[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#the-npm-install-and-audit)

The shapes with a front end (raw + Vue, Blade + Vue, Inertia) ship a `package-lock.json`, written against the template's `package.json` with npm's one-day release cooldown honored, so a fresh app's first pipeline installs exactly what Sourdough tested (BEST_PRACTICES 4.10). The `frontend` job runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which installs the lock as it is, runs no package's install script, and stops when `package.json` and the lock disagree, then `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`, which fails the job on a high or critical advisory in a runtime dependency (moderate and low ones are listed, not fatal), then a second `npm audit` that lists every finding, dev tools included, and never fails. The lock is seeded: after the bake it is yours, and npm writes it. Change a dependency with `npm install` and commit `package.json` and `package-lock.json` together. A package that truly needs its install script (a native addon, a binary download) gets an `npm rebuild <name>` line after `npm ci`, by name, so nothing else runs one.

### The bill of materials[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#the-bill-of-materials)

Preflight's `sbom` component writes `sbom.cdx.json`, a CycloneDX SBOM of the Composer packages `composer.lock` installs (dev packages left out), and keeps it for 30 days (BEST_PRACTICES 4.15). The shapes with a front end add the npm half in their `frontend` job: `@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm`, the CycloneDX project's own tool, pinned to an exact version and run with `--ignore-scripts`, writes `sbom-npm.cdx.json` from what the install put in `node_modules`, dev packages included, because the build tools make the bundle. npm's built-in `npm sbom` refuses a `package.json` without a `version`, which an app's never has. When the next advisory lands, the affected apps are one search per file away. Container image contents are not covered: the shapes build no image in CI.

### Secrets and deploy credentials[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#secrets-and-deploy-credentials)

Preflight's `secret-detection` component runs Gitleaks over the checkout and fails on anything shaped like a credential, redacted in the log and in `gitleaks.json`. A freshly baked app of every shape scans clean.

Citadel deploys an app with a Quick Update, so a baked pipeline holds no deploy credential and runs no deploy job (BEST_PRACTICES 6.5). Each shape ships the part a pipeline file can express, a hidden `.deploy` template for the day an app adds a deploy job:

```yaml
.deploy:
  stage: deploy
  resource_group: deploy
  interruptible: false
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: never
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_REF_PROTECTED == "true"
```

A job that extends it never runs for a merge request and runs only on a protected branch or tag, the only refs where GitLab hands a job its protected variables. One deploy runs at a time, and a newer pipeline never cancels one halfway. `tests/TemplateCiGatesTest.php` fails Sourdough's suite when a shape's job deploys (`stage: deploy` or `environment:`) without extending `.deploy`, when a component input references any variable but the GitLab host and `IMAGE_PREFIX`, or when the file sets a variable named like a credential.

The rest are project settings, so each generated README lists them under "Pipeline": protect `main` and the release tags; keep each deploy credential in a protected, masked (or masked and hidden) variable; never put a credential in the file or a component's inputs; keep the job token allowlist on and add other projects by name; read a fork's merge request before running its pipeline in the project; prefer the deploy target's own secret store for anything long-lived. All of it works on GitLab Community Edition. Protected environments, which would add an approval step, are a paid tier feature, so the file does not rely on them.

### Is the app still fed?[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#is-the-app-still-fed)

Every shape also ships a `sourdough-feed` job. It installs the newest Sourdough release (`composer create-project waynestate/sourdough`) on the shape's own `composer` image, through `${IMAGE_PREFIX}` and on the `.composer-cache`, and runs two checks against the app's manifest:

- `sourdough manifest --check` lists the managed files edited since the last bake or feed. Drift is normal (feed merges it), so the list is a report and never fails the job.
- `sourdough feed --dry-run` exits `1` when a newer release has template changes the app has not fed. The job exits `1` too, and `allow_failure: exit_codes: [1]` turns that into a warning: a pending feed never blocks a deploy.

Exit `2` from either (no manifest, a manifest from a newer Sourdough, conflict markers left over from the last feed, a bake that failed) fails the job, because the app's record needs fixing before any feed can run. The full table and the job itself are in [Keeping apps current](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/keeping-current.html#feed-in-ci).

### Dependency caching[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#dependency-caching)

A pipeline that downloads every image and package on every run can get the runner's address rate limited by Docker Hub, and a busy afternoon of fifty jobs can look like abuse. Every shape's `.gitlab-ci.yml` keeps those downloads cached, so a fed starter does not go asking the neighbors for flour.

**Images.** Each job's image is `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/<image>`, digest pins kept. `IMAGE_PREFIX` defaults to `docker.io`, and a `workflow:` rule sets it to the group's [GitLab Dependency Proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/packages/dependency_proxy/) (`$CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX`) when the GitLab has one. The runner signs in to the proxy on its own; the proxy asks Docker Hub once and serves its copy after that. The Preflight components (0.3.0 and later) put a prefix in front of their own default images themselves, through their `image_prefix` input; every shape hands them `image_prefix: "${IMAGE_PREFIX}"`, so components and jobs follow the same rule. The shapes pass no `image` input, so each component runs the default image its pinned release carries, pinned by digest.

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX
      variables:
        IMAGE_PREFIX: $CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX
    - when: always

variables:
  IMAGE_PREFIX: docker.io
```

On a group whose proxy is turned off, set `IMAGE_PREFIX` to `docker.io` in **Settings > CI/CD > Variables**: a project variable beats the file's own.

Warning

To run a component on another image, give its `image` input the plain name, such as `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:<digest>`, never `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/php:...`. The component already adds `image_prefix` in front, so a prefixed image is pulled from a path that does not exist and the job fails before it starts.

**Packages.** `COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` and `npm_config_cache` point at `.cache/composer/` and `.cache/npm/` inside the project, and every job that installs extends `.composer-cache` (keyed on `composer.lock`) or `.npm-cache` (keyed on `package-lock.json` and `package.json`). A lock change starts a fresh cache, and the install still resolves from the lock, so a cached run never gets a stale package.

The `a11y` component pulls Microsoft's Playwright image from mcr.microsoft.com, which the Dependency Proxy does not front, so it takes no `image_prefix`; the runner's own image cache is what keeps that pull rare.

`tests/TemplateCiCacheTest.php` fails Sourdough's own suite when a shape's own job gains an image without `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/` or an install without its cache, and `tests/PreflightPinTest.php` fails it when a shape pins another Preflight version than the rest, gives a component a prefixed `image`, or leaves out `image_prefix`.

### On GitHub[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#on-github)

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci`, pinned to Preflight 0.1.4: GitHub's copy of Preflight has no later tag yet, so the GitHub side stays there while GitLab runs 0.4.0.

### What green means[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#what-green-means)

Green means `composer ci` passed on all three PHP versions on both.

### The smoke jobs on CI[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#the-smoke-jobs-on-ci)

On CI the smoke gate runs as one job per shape: `smoke` (matrix) on GitHub, `smoke-raw`, `smoke-raw-vue`, `smoke-blade`, `smoke-blade-vue` and `smoke-inertia` on GitLab. All are `allow_failure: true` until the lead has seen every shape green on CI once; flip them to blocking after that proof. The full recipe is in [Testing](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html).

The `proof` job runs the whole [proof harness](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html) on GitLab: every shape and every oven, with the last release fed forward, and keeps the Last run table and every step log as an artifact. It never runs on a push: start it by hand from any pipeline, or from a pipeline schedule that sets `SOURDOUGH_PROOF` to `1`.
