## Wiring the stack in[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#wiring-the-stack-in)

Goal: know exactly what Sourdough wires into a freshly baked app, and why each piece is a default rather than an option. Read this before your first bake, and keep it at hand while you maintain an app. Like the starter it is named after, a Sourdough app only stays alive while something keeps feeding it; the wiring below is the first meal.

Sourdough is the app starter for the WSU stack. One command scaffolds a new app with SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), PROCTOR (checks), and the Preflight CI components already in place. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

![The proof: dough rises past its gold band as WayneUI, SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight go in one by one, over the feeding schedule](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/proof.svg)

*The proofing log from the front page: what goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`, and the day-to-day check that keeps it alive.*

### What lands in every app[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#what-lands-in-every-app)

Every generated app has SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR as a dev dependency, a `.gitlab-ci.yml` that includes the Preflight components, a `/up` route that does not touch the database, and a README that points at the CREED handbook. The libraries are tagged (SESAME, HELMET with a health check, PROCTOR, Preflight templates), and `sourdough new` wires them into every generated app.

Defaults decide what most apps end up doing, so the stack is wired in by default, not as an option. Laravel's own kits include sign-in, rate limiting and two-factor login out of the box for the same reason.

For the Playbook and ADVISOR wiring and the flags that turn each one off, see [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

### The release script runs the check, but do not call it the gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#the-release-script-runs-the-check-but-do-not-call-it-the-gate)

The Citadel release script asks PROCTOR's deploy gate (`proctor gate`, from Squire's kit 0.9.0 and PROCTOR 0.8, graded on the PHP that runs the release) for a go or no-go, ratcheted against the last release that went on, so a failure that is already live is held and only a new one blocks. By default it only reports a no-go; `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce` stops the release on one, before the frontend build and the migrations. Treat it as a report either way. The kit adds two more report-only moves: after the optimize step the script restarts Laravel's long-lived processes (`php artisan reload`, or `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt` on an older Laravel; `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0` turns it off), and the image drops shell functions from the web's PHP (`SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS`), turns on production opcache (`SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE`), answers `ServerTokens Prod` and reads secrets from `/run/secrets`. Since kit 0.9.0 a Laravel release also stops before anything installs when `APP_KEY` is unset or `APP_DEBUG` is on in production (best practice 4.14). A failure in a release script cannot stop bad code from going live on a Quick Update, so the real gates are CI before merge and, later, a platform check.

Warning

Promising a gate that does not hold is worse than having none. Nothing prevents someone from describing the script as a gate in a README.

### Keep the start-up path small and boring[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#keep-the-start-up-path-small-and-boring)

Generated commands should run and exit on their own, with no prompts and no network calls after install. Developers, CI and coding agents all run them, and a prompt that waits for input breaks all three.

### Accessibility gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#accessibility-gate)

The US Justice Department's Title II web rule sets WCAG 2.1 Level AA for state and local government web content. An interim final rule published on 2026-04-20 moved the first compliance date to 2027-04-26 for entities of 50,000 people or more and to 2028-04-26 for smaller ones. The standard and the ongoing duty to keep content accessible did not change. Whether and when the rule applies to a given WSU app is not decided here; ask WSU's accessibility office.

What Sourdough ships: every shape's pipeline renders the app's own pages and checks them with Preflight's `a11y` component at WCAG 2.2 AA (which includes 2.1 AA), blocking. The Laravel shapes check the home page signed out and the dashboard signed in through `/login`; the raw shapes check their one page, signed in by SESAME's fake driver, and raw + Vue saves `/api/me` so its Vue app draws the signed-in view. In production the sign-in page itself is the CAS server's. WayneUI's accessible templates are the default markup, and Sourdough's own pipeline runs the same component over every page under `site/`, so the "new app" page passes the gate when it lands there. How the pages are saved is in [CI](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#the-accessibility-gate).

Note

Automated checks find only part of the problems, and every generated README says so. axe-core checks a loaded page, so the Vue paths' focus after navigation and announced route changes still need a person with a keyboard and a screen reader.

### Protect deploy credentials in the generated pipeline[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#protect-deploy-credentials-in-the-generated-pipeline)

GitLab's docs say masking a variable does not reliably stop a malicious user from reading it; protected variables exist only in pipelines on protected branches and tags; a pipeline for a merge request from a fork should run in the parent project only after review, because malicious code can compromise masked and protected variables; and sensitive values belong in an external secrets manager. A project's job-token allowlist includes only the project itself by default, and GitLab calls disabling it a security risk. From GitLab 19.0 job tokens use the JWT format by default, and the legacy format is available only until 20.0.

What Sourdough ships: Citadel deploys by Quick Update, so a generated pipeline holds no credential and runs no deploy job. Each shape carries a `.deploy` template (no merge request pipelines, protected refs only, one deploy at a time) for the day an app adds one, Preflight's `secret-detection` component (Gitleaks) fails a pipeline that commits a credential, and Sourdough's suite fails when a shape's job deploys without `.deploy`, a component input carries a variable other than the host and `IMAGE_PREFIX`, or the file sets a variable named like a credential. The settings a file cannot hold are a checklist in every generated README: protected `main` and tags, protected and masked variables, the job-token allowlist on with projects added by name, fork merge requests read before they run, and the deploy target's own secret store for anything long-lived. Details in [CI](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ci.html#secrets-and-deploy-credentials).

Danger

Sensitive values belong in an external secrets manager. Put no secrets in component `inputs`, and run deploy jobs only on a protected branch or tag with protected variables.

### Where the code lives[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#where-the-code-lives)

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/sourdough) on git.wayne.edu. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it. git.wayne.edu is the starter culture now; GitHub is the slice Packagist eats.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html#related)

- [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html)

## Sourdough[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#sourdough)

![php](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![exit codes](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/exit-codes.svg) [GitHub CI](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Feed it and it grows.**

A starter you feed: `sourdough new` makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in. It starts every app shape: raw PHP, raw PHP with a Vue SPA, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with Blade and Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue ([WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) is that last shape already built). One command scaffolds a new app with WayneUI (the interface), SESAME (auth), HELMET (baseline runtime), Pinstripe (coding standard), PROCTOR (checks), the Preflight CI components, Squire's deploy files and ADVISOR (the stack's MCP server) already in place, with its PHP floor read from CREED's policy. It is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Every loaf gets proofed before it ships. Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

![The proof: dough rises past its gold band as WayneUI, SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR and Preflight go in one by one, over the feeding schedule](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/proof.svg)

The proofing log from the front page: what goes into the tub when you run `sourdough new`, and the day-to-day check that keeps it alive.

### Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install)

```
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

After `composer global require`, the `sourdough` command lives in `composer global config bin-dir --absolute`; put that directory on your PATH. Or scaffold without installing, with `composer create-project waynestate/sourdough`. The full instructions are on [Install](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html).

### First run[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#first-run)

```
sourdough new my-app
```

Expected: exit code `0` (done), a `my-app` directory holding a Wayne State app with the stack wired in, and Next steps printed for it. Then run the app's own gate from inside `my-app/`:

```
composer ci
```

The step-by-step version is the [Quick start](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

### Pick your path[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bake your first app and run its checks.
- [Install](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): what the machine needs, and the two ways to get Sourdough.
- [Reference](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): every command and option, the plan format, the templates.

### Status[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Version 0.2.0 (2026-11-08), MIT license. Main carries more since then (Squire 0.10.0's kit, Preflight 0.4.0 pins, `/ready` that asks the database and the cache): the [changelog](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html) lists it under Unreleased, and [Upgrading](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html) says what a feed brings. Agents: this site ships [llms.txt](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) for LLM readers.

## Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

Sourdough is one PHP command, so it works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Requirements[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- PHP 8.3 or newer (`^8.3` in `composer.json`).
- Composer, for the install lines below.
- No PHP extensions are declared in `composer.json`.

Where the code lives: the canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/sourdough) on git.wayne.edu. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it. git.wayne.edu is the starter culture now; GitHub is the slice Packagist eats.

### Install[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Two ways in: install the `sourdough` command on your machine, or scaffold without installing.

composer global require

```bash
composer global require waynestate/sourdough
```

composer create-project

```bash
composer create-project waynestate/sourdough
```

Note

After `composer global require`, the `sourdough` command lives in `composer global config bin-dir --absolute`; put that directory on your PATH.

### Verify[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

```bash
sourdough --version
```

Expected:

```
Sourdough 0.2.0
```

The CLI is a Symfony Console application named Sourdough, version 0.2.0 (`bin/sourdough`), so `--version` prints the name and the version.

### Next steps[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): bake your first app and run its checks.
- [Pick a shape](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/shapes.html): choose the permutation your app needs.
- [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html): every flag `sourdough new` accepts.

## MAINTAINING: feeding the starter[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#maintaining-feeding-the-starter)

How to build, test, release and keep Sourdough alive. Sourdough makes a Wayne State app with the stack already wired in and is meant to own that wiring for the app's whole life. Built today: `new` and `new --describe`, `manifest` and `feed`. Planned: `adopt`. Like any starter, it needs regular feeding, or it goes flat.

### What Sourdough is and what it depends on[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#what-sourdough-is-and-what-it-depends-on)

- `waynestate/sourdough` on Packagist, with the CLI `bin/sourdough`.
- Runtime dependencies: `symfony/console`, `symfony/http-client`, `justinrainbow/json-schema`, `openai-php/client` (only for `new --describe`, which can ask an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan; optional). No other stack package at runtime.
- **Generated apps** require `waynestate/helmet`, `waynestate/sesame` and `waynestate/proctor` from Packagist.
- **It carries a copy of Squire's templates** in `templates/squire/` (`raw/`, `laravel/`, `static/`, `vue/`, `catalog.json`, `manifest.json`). Squire owns those files; Sourdough never hand-edits them. `composer squire-copy:sync` rewrites the copy from the installed `waynestate/squire` package (dev dependency `^0.7`), and `composer squire-copy:check` (part of `composer ci`) exits 1 when the committed copy has drifted.
- `feed` needs only git on the developer's machine: it bakes the app's shape again with the manifest's answers and three-way merges each file with `git merge-file`, the base found by its manifest hash in `.sourdough/base/` or the app's git history (see `docs/guides/keeping-current.md`). `new` and `feed` bake through the same `Baker`, so a change to a generator reaches both.

### Where it lives[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#where-it-lives)

Development happens on git.wayne.edu, the canonical repository ([enterprise-apps/sourdough](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/sourdough)). GitHub ([waynestate/sourdough](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough)) is a read-only push mirror: `main` and tags are copied automatically, nobody pushes to it, and Packagist picks releases up from there. Changes, issues and merge requests go to git.wayne.edu.

### Build and test[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#build-and-test)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| Only the tests | `composer test` |
| Fix code style | `composer fix` |
| Check the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:check` |
| Refresh the Squire copy | `composer squire-copy:sync`, then commit `templates/squire/` |
| Try a generation | `php bin/sourdough new ./demo --raw --dry-run` |

With only Docker (the same lines work in PowerShell and sh):

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

The `stack-composer-cache` volume keeps Composer's downloads between runs; Docker creates it the first time.

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan, the Squire copy check, the agent-ready files check, the docs site check and `composer audit`.

### CI[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5) and `composer-audit` components, plus a `composer-ci` job.
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci`, pinned to Preflight 0.1.4: GitHub's copy of Preflight has no later tag yet, so the GitHub side stays there while GitLab runs 0.4.0.
- Green means `composer ci` passed on all three PHP versions on both.

### Smoke gate[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#smoke-gate)

The smoke gate is the proofing bench: it proofs one shape at a time before that shape may be claimed. It bakes the app with this checkout's own `bin/sourdough new <dir> --no-advisor --no-playbook --no-input` (the CLI under test is the one being shipped). Every bake passes `--no-playbook`, because Playbook is the default wiring but its package is private on git.wayne.edu and the gate must run credential-free.

Right after the bake, every shape proves its manifest and its bake: `sourdough manifest --check` must be clean, and with the fresh app committed to a scratch git repository `sourdough feed --dry-run` must find nothing to feed (a bake that is not stable would make every feed of it a conflict). The repository is dropped again before the app's own checks:

- `raw`: `composer install`, `composer test`, `composer proctor` and `composer ci`, then a live check: fetch the pinned WayneUI release once into `public/wayne-ui.php`, start the app with `APP_ENV=local` and expect `/` 200 with the app's home page in WayneUI's shell, `/nope` 404 and `/up` 200 (the front controller defaults `APP_ENV` to production when it is unset, so the server must set it)
- `raw-vue`: the raw steps plus `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (from the shipped `package-lock.json`) and `npm run build`, then the same live server, which must answer `/` with the built app mounted on `id="app"`, `/api/me` with the signed-in user (and `401` without a session), `/nope` with `404` and the app, and `/up` with `200`
- `blade`: `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `php artisan test`, `composer proctor` and `composer ci`, then Laravel's own router (the one `php artisan serve` runs) must answer `/` with the Blade home page, `/dashboard` after SESAME's fake sign-in, `/nope` with `404` and `/up` with `200`
- `blade-vue`: the blade steps with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run build` before the tests; `/` must also load the built assets and `/dashboard` carry the Vue island
- `inertia`: the blade-vue steps plus `npm run typecheck`; `/` must hand Vue the Inertia `Home` page and `/dashboard` the `Dashboard` page

With `--sail` or `--docker` after the shape (`smoke-shape.sh blade --docker`), a Laravel shape proves its oven instead: the scaffold's files are there, then `composer install`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan test` and `composer proctor`. The gate never lights the oven: it has no Docker daemon.

With `SMOKE_FEED_FROM` set to a release (for example `0.1.6`), the gate also bakes the shape with that release from Packagist, commits it, and feeds it forward with this checkout: no conflict, a clean manifest afterwards, nothing left to feed. `scripts/proof.sh` (`scripts/proof.ps1` on Windows) runs every shape and every oven this way, one after another, and writes the Last run table on the [Proof](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html) page.

Each step prints `ok`; the first `FAIL` stops the run and shows the command's tail. A shape is claimed in the docs only when its smoke is green.

Run it per OS. The image (`scripts/smoke.Dockerfile`) pins php 8.5, composer 2 and node 22, so the bake is identical everywhere:

Linux and macOS:

```
docker build -f scripts/smoke.Dockerfile -t sourdough-smoke:local .
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo:ro" -v /work -e SMOKE_WORK=/work sourdough-smoke:local sh /repo/scripts/smoke-shape.sh <shape>
```

Windows PowerShell:

```
.\scripts\smoke-shape.ps1 <shape>
```

The PowerShell wrapper builds the same image once and reuses it. Pass `-WorkDir <dir>` to bind a local folder to `/work` so the scratch copy, the generated app and the per-step logs survive the run.

Environment variables:

- `SMOKE_WORK`: the scratch dir for the copy, the app and the logs. Defaults to a fresh temp dir that is removed on exit.
- `SMOKE_KEEP`: set to `1` to keep the scratch dir behind for inspection.
- `SMOKE_FEED_FROM`: a released Sourdough to bake and feed forward (off when unset).
- `SMOKE_PREV_CACHE`: where that release is installed, so several runs share one copy.
- `SMOKE_PORT`: the live server's port (default `8099`).

On CI the gate runs as one job per shape: `smoke` (matrix) on GitHub, `smoke-raw`, `smoke-raw-vue`, `smoke-blade`, `smoke-blade-vue` and `smoke-inertia` on GitLab. All are `allow_failure: true` until the lead has seen every shape green on CI once; flip them to blocking after that proof. The whole proof runs in the GitLab `proof` job, by hand or on a schedule that sets `SOURDOUGH_PROOF` to `1`, never on a push.

### The local runtime output (Sail and Docker)[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#the-local-runtime-output-sail-and-docker)

The `--sail` and `--docker` output is checked by tests and by the proof's oven runs: `tests/SailScaffoldTest.php` and `tests/DockerScaffoldTest.php` assert on the files each scaffold writes, including real-binary runs through `bin/sourdough`, and `scripts/proof.sh` bakes every Laravel shape in each oven, installs it and runs its suite and PROCTOR. No Docker daemon is part of either, so a bake with `--docker` is not proven to boot here. The plan is to add Docker smoke runs to the smoke gate once it can drive a compose stack (build the app image, start MySQL, run `php artisan migrate` and expect `/up` 200); until then the docs claim what the tests prove.

The base images in `templates/docker/Dockerfile` are pinned by manifest-list digest, so one pin resolves natively on amd64 and arm64. To bump a pin:

1. Run `docker buildx imagetools inspect <tag>` for the tag you want (for example `php:8.5-cli-trixie`) and copy the manifest-list digest, the `sha256:` value on the top `Digest:` line, not the per-architecture digests listed below it.
2. Replace the digest on the matching `FROM` line, add a CHANGELOG line, and commit.

A digest pin never moves on its own, so schedule these bumps (for example when a new patch release lands on the line) to pick up security fixes inside the image.

### Refreshing the Squire templates[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#refreshing-the-squire-templates)

When Squire's templates change, regenerate the copy from a Squire checkout, then verify it:

```
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire
php ../squire/bin/export-templates.php --to=../sourdough/templates/squire --check
```

Commit the refreshed copy with the Squire commit in the message, and add a CHANGELOG line. Apps generated earlier pick up the refreshed files with their next `sourdough feed`.

### Refreshing a template's lock file[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#refreshing-a-template-s-lock-file)

Each template that ships a `package.json` (`raw-vue`, `laravel-blade-vue`, `laravel-inertia`) ships the `package-lock.json` that goes with it, so a fresh app passes `npm ci` on its first pipeline. `tests/TemplateNpmLockTest.php` fails when the two drift. After editing a template's `package.json`, write its lock again in the pinned Node image the pipelines use (`node:22.21.1-alpine3.22`, by digest), in a scratch folder that holds a copy of that `package.json` and of `templates/squire/vue/.npmrc`:

```
sed -i 's/{{app_slug}}/app-slug-placeholder/' package.json
npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --before=<yesterday, as 2026-11-07T00:00:00Z>
sed 's/"app-slug-placeholder"/"{{app_slug}}"/g' package-lock.json > <repo>/templates/<shape>/package-lock.json
```

The stand-in name keeps npm away from the `{{app_slug}}` placeholder, which is not a valid package name. `--before` keeps the one-day release cooldown the app's `.npmrc` sets, which npm 10 ignores. Then run `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev` and `npm run build` on a bake of the shape (the smoke jobs run the install and the build), and commit the lock with its `package.json`. Apps already baked keep their own lock: it is seeded.

### What belongs here[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#what-belongs-here)

If every app should have something, it goes in Sourdough's templates. If only the Laravel + Inertia/Vue shape (WELD) should have it, it lives in WELD. Version rules belong to CREED, checks to PROCTOR, Citadel scripts to Squire.

### Releasing[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#releasing)

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. `composer ci` and the Squire copy check green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
3. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu, with an approver. The push mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### The front page[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#the-front-page)

`site/` is the static front page, for `https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/` on Citadel, served through a small raw-PHP `deploy/` layer generated with Squire.

### Things that trip people up[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#things-that-trip-people-up)

- In 0.1 all five shapes generate. `--raw --vue` apps need `npm run build` (or `npm run dev`) before `/` renders: `src/Vite.php` refuses with a plain message when there is neither a build nor a dev server.
- Commit `.sourdough/manifest.json` (and `.sourdough/base/`) in generated apps; `feed` needs them.

### Who maintains it[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/maintaining.html#who-maintains-it)

Adam Perkins, Wayne State University Enterprise Applications. Internal runbook (accounts, tokens, mirrors, deploy access): ask Enterprise Applications.

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

Reference for the `sourdough` CLI: every command, argument, option and exit code, exactly as the sources define them. For the JSON plan behind `--describe` and `--plan`, see [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html).

### sourdough new[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#sourdough-new)

Make a new Wayne State app with the stack already wired in.

```
sourdough new [dir] [options]
```

`dir` is the directory to create the app in. It is required unless you use `--describe`.

#### Options[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options)

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--raw` | use the raw PHP base |
| `--laravel` | use the Laravel base |
| `--vue` | add a Vue front end |
| `--inertia` | use Inertia/Vue (implies `--laravel`) |
| `--sail` | run the Laravel app on Sail for local work (compose.yaml; needs WSL2 on Windows) |
| `--docker` | generate a Dockerfile and compose.yaml for local work (native on every OS; amd64 and arm64) |
| `--dry-run` | print the plan and write nothing |
| `--name` | app name (default: the basename of `<dir>`) |
| `--no-input` | never prompt (Sourdough has no prompts) |
| `--json` | with `--dry-run`, print the plan as JSON |
| `--describe "<sentence>"` | describe what the app does; a model plans it (needs the `SOURDOUGH_LLM_*` env vars) |
| `--plan-only` | with `--describe`, print the plan as JSON and write nothing |
| `--plan <file>` | a ready-made plan file (JSON, or YAML ending in `.yaml` or `.yml`, matching `resources/plan.schema.json`), such as the `.sourdough/plan.yaml` every bake saves |
| `--playbook` | kept for compatibility: Playbook is now the default |
| `--no-playbook` | skip the Playbook wiring (for CI and automated tests only; WSU apps need Playbook) |
| `--no-advisor` | skip the ADVISOR wiring (no `require-dev` entry, no `.mcp.json` git-ignore line of its own, no README section; the Laravel shapes still ignore `/.mcp.json` for Laravel Boost) |

Note

`--sail` and `--docker` are both real for the Laravel shapes (`--laravel`, `--laravel --vue` and `--inertia`) and mutually exclusive: together they are refused with `Choose one of --sail or --docker, not both.` (exit `1`). With `--sail` the app runs on Laravel Sail: `laravel/sail` in require-dev, a `compose.yaml`, the database settings in `.env.example` and a README section; the database is MySQL 8.4 LTS. On Windows, Sail needs WSL2, and `--docker` is the route that works natively. With `--docker` Sourdough writes the app's own Docker setup after the shape is baked: a two-target `Dockerfile` (dev and prod) whose base images are pinned by manifest-list digest, a `compose.yaml` with a MySQL 8.4 service (and a vite service for the Vue and Inertia shapes), a `.dockerignore`, the PHP ini files the image copies in, the `composer dev-up`, `dev-down` and `dev-shell` scripts, the database settings in `.env.example`, and a "Run it locally with Docker" README section. It works natively on Windows, macOS and Linux (no WSL2 needed) and is checked on amd64 and arm64. Playbook credentials reach a production build only as a BuildKit secret, never a build arg. The raw paths keep their own refusal at the plan step: "`--sail` and `--docker` are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP."

#### Exit codes[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

Exit codes: `0` done, `1` refused (invalid flags, non-empty target, not available, model gave up), `2` tool error.

| Refused case | Exact message | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--describe` and `--plan` together | `--describe and --plan are mutually exclusive.` | `1` |
| `--sail` and `--docker` together | `Choose one of --sail or --docker, not both.` | `1` |
| `--sail` or `--docker` with a raw permutation | `--sail and --docker are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP.` | `1` |
| `--playbook` and `--no-playbook` together | `--playbook and --no-playbook are mutually exclusive.` | `1` |
| `--plan-only` without `--describe` | `--plan-only is only available with --describe.` | `1` |
| `dir` missing without `--describe` | `The dir argument is required unless you use --describe.` | `1` |
| no read access to Playbook | `You need read access to Playbook (a private package on git.wayne.edu) to make a Wayne State app.` plus the how-to | `1` |
| `--json` without `--dry-run` | `--json is only available with --dry-run.` | `2` |
| the model could not be reached (`--describe`) | `The model could not be reached:` plus the underlying error | `2` |

Other refusals, all exit `1`: invalid flags, a non-empty target, a model that gives up (the message points to `--plan=<file>`), and an app name that fails validation.

#### Playbook access check[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#playbook-access-check)

By default the generated app requires `waynestate/playbook` (WSU's private shared-values package on git.wayne.edu): the VCS repository, the package in `require`, `config.gitlab-domains` so Composer sends your token to git.wayne.edu, the seven setting names in `.env.example`, a `composer playbook` script that shows whether Playbook is installed, and a "WSU values (PLAYBOOK)" README section that explains how to get read access.

Before writing anything, `sourdough new` checks that this machine can read the package (a Composer credential, then a direct git probe):

| Situation | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| no read access | refuses with exit `1` and prints the how-to |
| git.wayne.edu unreachable | still generates the app, but warns that `composer install` will need the connection |
| non-interactive run or CI environment | skips the check |
| `--dry-run` | runs the check but never refuses; the JSON plan carries a `playbook` key with the mode, the access status and the probe that answered |

After generation the Next steps point at `composer playbook`. `--playbook` is kept for compatibility and changes nothing; `--no-playbook` skips all of it. The two flags together are refused with exit `1`.

#### ADVISOR wiring[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#advisor-wiring)

Generated apps ship with ADVISOR wired in by default: `waynestate/advisor` lands in `require-dev`, `.mcp.json` is git-ignored (a client config starts a program for whoever opens the project), and the README gains an "ADVISOR" section. The Next steps print the install line once dependencies are in:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
```

`--no-advisor` skips all of it.

The three Laravel shapes also ship Laravel Boost as a dev-only tool, whatever the ADVISOR answer: `laravel/boost` in `require-dev`, a guarded `composer boost-update` after `composer update`, a `.gitignore` block for what `php artisan boost:install` writes (`/.mcp.json`, `/boost.json`, `/CLAUDE.md`, `/AGENTS.md`, `/.claude/skills/`, `/.junie/`), the stack's guidelines and two starter rules in `.ai/`, and `tests/Feature/BoostDevOnlyTest.php`. ADVISOR complements Boost: Boost knows Laravel, ADVISOR knows the stack. See [Laravel Boost, dev only](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#laravel-boost-dev-only).

#### App name validation[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#app-name-validation)

The app name (from `--name`, from the plan, or from the basename of `<dir>`) must start with a letter or number and use only letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores, at most 63 characters; anything else is refused before anything is written.

#### PHP floor and support lines[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#php-floor-and-support-lines)

Every plan, dry run or real, prints two lines under `Target:`:

```
PHP:         PHP ^8.3, tested on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (from waynestate/creed, refreshed 2026-10-29)
Support:     supported, owned by Sourdough maintainers; Laravel 13 gets security fixes until 2028-03-17
```

The floor comes from CREED's policy at bake time; when the policy cannot be read, the first line ends `(pinned fallback: <reason>)` and the bake uses the pinned values. A shape that is deprecated also prints `Deprecated: The <shape> shape is deprecated since Sourdough <x> and is removed in <y>; move to <shape>. See <page>` to stderr; it never changes the exit code. With `--dry-run --json` the plan gains a `php` object and a `support` object with the same facts. See [Support and sunset](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/support.html).

#### Environment[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#environment)

- `SOURDOUGH_POLICY`: a CREED-format `policy.json` to take the PHP floor from (default: the copy installed with `waynestate/creed`). A file that cannot be read means the pinned fallback, named in the `PHP:` line.
- `SOURDOUGH_COMPOSER`: the Composer binary the Laravel shapes bake their skeleton with (default: `composer` on PATH).
- `SOURDOUGH_LLM_BASE_URL`, `SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY`, `SOURDOUGH_LLM_MODEL`: the model `--describe` asks.

#### Next steps printed after generation[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#next-steps-printed-after-generation)

| Shape | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| Raw PHP | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `composer serve` |
| Laravel + Blade | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `php artisan key:generate`, `php artisan migrate`, `php artisan serve` |
| Laravel + Blade + Vue islands | the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build` |
| Laravel + Inertia/Vue | the Laravel + Blade steps plus `npm install` and `npm run build` |
| any Laravel shape with `--sail` | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `./vendor/bin/sail up -d`, `./vendor/bin/sail artisan key:generate`, `./vendor/bin/sail artisan migrate`, `(Windows: run sail from WSL2, or use --docker)`; the Vue and Inertia shapes add `./vendor/bin/sail npm install` and `./vendor/bin/sail npm run dev` |
| any Laravel shape with `--docker` | `cd <dir>`, `composer install`, `cp .env.example .env`, `composer dev-up`, `docker compose exec app php artisan key:generate`, `docker compose exec app php artisan migrate`; the Vue and Inertia shapes end with `(Vite runs as its own service on port 5173)` |

With ADVISOR wired in, `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write` is printed after `composer install`. With Playbook required, the output ends with: `WSU values: Playbook installs with composer install. Check it any time with: composer playbook`.

### sourdough manifest[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#sourdough-manifest)

Check a generated app against its Sourdough manifest.

```
sourdough manifest [dir] [--check]
```

| Argument or option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dir` | the app directory to check (default: the current directory) |
| `--check` | list managed files that changed or are missing; exit 1 when anything changed |

Without `--check` the command answers "Use `sourdough manifest --check` to check the app against its manifest." and exits `2`.

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` changed or missing, `2` tool error.

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Clean: every managed file matches the manifest.` | every managed file matches the manifest |
| `changed <file>` | a managed file changed |
| `missing <file>` | a managed file is missing |

Seeded files are never reported: the app owns them. Line endings are forgiven: a CRLF checkout of a file Sourdough wrote with LF is not `changed`.

### sourdough feed[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#sourdough-feed)

Bring Sourdough template updates into an app without clobbering what it has changed.

```
sourdough feed [dir] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

| Argument or option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dir` | the app directory to feed (default: the current directory) |
| `--dry-run` | print the plan and write nothing; exit `1` when feeding would change files |
| `--json` | print the plan, or the result, as JSON |

Feed bakes the app's shape again with the answers in its manifest, compares the base (what the manifest recorded), the app and the new loaf file by file, and writes the result. How it decides, and where the base comes from, is in [Keeping apps current](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/keeping-current.html#what-feed-does).

#### Plan lines[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#plan-lines)

One line per file that changes, ` <action> <file> (<why>)`; files feed leaves alone are not listed.

| Action | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | new in the template (or a seeded file new to the template, where the app has none) |
| `update` | the template changed it and the app had not: replaced |
| `merge` | both changed it in different places: three-way merged by `git merge-file` |
| `conflict` | both changed the same lines, there was no base to merge from, or the file is binary: marked, never overwritten |
| `remove` | the template dropped it and the app had not changed it |
| `keep` | the template dropped a file the app changed (it is the app's now), or changed a file the app deleted (it stays deleted) |
| `record` | the app already has the template's new version of the file: nothing is written, the manifest records it |

An app baked by Sourdough 0.1.6 with `--sail` or `--docker` has no oven in its manifest's answers (0.1.6 wrote the manifest before the oven's scaffold ran). Feed reads the oven from the app's files instead (a `Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml` and the `dev-up` script for Docker; `laravel/sail` and Sail's `compose.yaml` for Sail), says so in a `note:` line, and records the oven's files, so `sourdough manifest --check` is clean afterwards.

A conflict in a text file holds git's markers, `<<<<<<< app`, `=======` and `>>>>>>> sourdough <version>`; a binary conflict leaves the template's copy next to the app's as `<file>.sourdough-new`.

After the plan lines: how many base copies feed keeps in `.sourdough/base/`, a one-line count per action, and the next steps. A real feed ends with the undo line: `To undo the whole feed: git restore . && git clean -fd (the tree was clean before it ran).`

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Fresh: the app already has everything Sourdough <version> bakes into a <template> app. Nothing to feed.` | nothing to do; nothing written, not even the manifest |
| `note: Not inside a git repository: ...` | dry runs only: a real feed would refuse |
| `note: Uncommitted changes: ...` | dry runs only: a real feed would refuse until the tree is clean |

#### Exit codes[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes-1)

| Run | `0` | `1` | `2` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourdough feed` | fed cleanly, or nothing to feed | fed, with conflicts to resolve | tool error |
| `sourdough feed --dry-run` | fresh | feeding would change files | tool error |

| Tool error | Message starts with | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no manifest in the directory | `No Sourdough manifest found in "<dir>".` | `2` |
| git is not on PATH | `sourdough feed needs git on PATH` | `2` |
| the app is not inside a git repository (real run) | `sourdough feed only runs inside a git repository` | `2` |
| uncommitted or untracked changes (real run) | `Commit or stash your changes first` | `2` |
| conflict markers or `.sourdough-new` copies left from the last feed | `Finish the last feed first` | `2` |
| the manifest was written by a newer Sourdough | `This app was fed by Sourdough <version>, newer than this one` | `2` |
| the manifest names a template this Sourdough does not bake | `The manifest names the template` | `2` |
| the manifest lists a path outside the app | `The manifest lists an unsafe path` | `2` |
| the bake failed (for example, Composer could not fetch the Laravel skeleton) | `sourdough feed failed:` | `2` |

#### JSON[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#json)

`--json` prints one object: `dir`, `template`, `from` and `to` (the Sourdough versions), `dry_run`, `fresh`, `files` (one `{path, action, detail}` per plan line), `summary` (a count per action), `base_copies` (the files kept in `.sourdough/base/`), `notes`, and `exit`. A deprecated shape's notice is one of the `notes` on every run; feeding an app whose shape was removed stops with exit `2` and names the replacement. See [Support and sunset](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/support.html).

#### Environment[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#environment-1)

- `SOURDOUGH_GIT`: the git binary to run (default: `git` on PATH).
- `SOURDOUGH_COMPOSER`: the Composer binary the Laravel shapes bake their skeleton with (default: `composer` on PATH), as for `sourdough new`.
- `SOURDOUGH_POLICY`: the CREED policy the new loaf takes its PHP floor from, as for `sourdough new`. Feed with the same policy the app was baked with, or the floor shows up as a template change.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#related)

- [Keeping apps current](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/keeping-current.html)
- [Plan format](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html)
- [Wiring the stack in](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html)

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html

## Plan format[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#plan-format)

Reference for the plan that `sourdough new --describe` asks a model for, `sourdough new --plan <file>` reads back (as JSON, or as YAML), and every bake saves in the app as `.sourdough/plan.yaml`. Every plan is validated against `resources/plan.schema.json`. For the flags that produce a plan, see [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

### The plan object[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-plan-object)

A plan is a small JSON object:

```json
{
    "permutation": "raw",
    "parts": ["sesame", "helmet"],
    "name": "my-app",
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "Post",
            "fields": [
                { "name": "title", "type": "string" },
                { "name": "body", "type": "text" }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "pages": ["/", "/posts"]
}
```

`permutation`, `parts`, and `name` are required; `models` and `pages` are optional.

| Key | Required | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permutation` | yes | one of the five permutation values below |
| `parts` | yes | a subset of `sesame`, `helmet`, `proctor`, and `preflight` |
| `name` | yes | the app name |
| `models` | no | a list of model objects |
| `pages` | no | a list of page paths, such as `/` and `/posts` |

When a plan is printed as JSON, empty `models` and `pages` are omitted.

#### Permutation values[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#permutation-values)

| Value | Flags | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | (none) or `--raw` | Raw PHP with WayneUI's standalone path |
| `raw-vue` | `--raw --vue` | Raw PHP + Vue SPA over JSON |
| `laravel-blade` | `--laravel` | Laravel + Blade |
| `laravel-blade-vue` | `--laravel --vue` | Laravel + Blade + Vue islands |
| `laravel-inertia` | `--laravel --inertia` (or `--inertia`) | Laravel + Inertia/Vue |

Flag resolution, from `src/Permutation.php`:

- `--inertia` implies `--laravel`: Inertia here means Laravel.
- `--raw` and `--laravel` are mutually exclusive: pick one base.
- `--vue` is not needed with `--inertia`: Inertia already means Vue.
- Combinations that make no sense are refused with an error that names the five shapes and their flags.

In 0.1 all five permutations generate.

#### Parts[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#parts)

From `src/Part.php`, the stack parts a Sourdough app is wired with:

| Value | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `sesame` | SESAME (auth) |
| `helmet` | HELMET (baseline runtime) |
| `proctor` | PROCTOR (checks) |
| `preflight` | the Preflight CI components |

A plan's `parts` is a subset of these.

#### Models[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#models)

Each model object has a `name` and a `fields` list; each field has a `name` and a `type`, both strings, as in the example above.

#### Pages[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#pages)

A list of strings, such as `["/", "/posts"]`.

### The saved plan[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-saved-plan)

Every bake saves its plan in the app as `.sourdough/plan.yaml`, next to the manifest (ADR-0014, decision 3): the recipe card taped inside the jar's lid. It is written after the bake succeeds, on both paths that bake:

| How you baked | What the saved plan holds |
| --- | --- |
| `--plan <file>` | that plan, with the name the app was baked with (`--name` wins over the plan's `name`) |
| flags (`--raw`, `--laravel`, `--vue`, `--inertia`) | the shape, the name, and all four parts, because every shape wires all four in |

`--dry-run` and a refused bake write nothing, so they save no plan. `--describe` prints a plan and writes nothing (generation from a description is not built yet), so it saves none either; pass its plan with `--plan` and that bake saves it. The plan from the example above is saved as:

```yaml
# The plan this app was baked from, saved by sourdough new (ADR-0014).
# It matches Sourdough's plan schema, so it bakes the same shape again:
#   sourdough new <dir> --plan=.sourdough/plan.yaml
# Sourdough never rewrites it after the bake: sourdough feed and
# sourdough manifest --check leave it alone. Commit it with the app.

permutation: raw
parts:
  - sesame
  - helmet
name: my-app
models:
  - name: Post
    fields:
      - { name: title, type: string }
      - { name: body, type: text }
pages:
  - /
  - /posts
```

The keys are the plan object's, in the same order, and the comment lines are YAML comments, so the file still matches the schema (which allows no extra keys). `--plan` reads a file ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` as YAML and anything else as JSON, through the same schema, so the saved plan bakes the same loaf again:

```bash
sourdough new my-app-copy --plan my-app/.sourdough/plan.yaml
```

#### Neither managed nor seeded[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#neither-managed-nor-seeded)

The saved plan is not in the manifest. The manifest lists the files the template wrote, and the plan is not template output: it is what you asked for. Like the manifest itself and `.sourdough/base/`, it is Sourdough's record about the app, not a file of the app, so it carries neither class:

- `sourdough manifest --check` never reports it, however you edit it.
- `sourdough feed` never reads, rewrites or removes it. Feed bakes from the shape and answers in the manifest, so an edited plan changes nothing a feed does, and an app baked before the plan was saved (Sourdough 0.1.7 and earlier) gets no plan written for it: feed does not guess at what nobody wrote down.

Edit it as the app grows (a new model, a new page), so it stays the record of what the app is for, and commit it with the manifest.

### Getting a plan[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#getting-a-plan)

Instead of choosing flags, describe what the app does and let a model plan it:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments"
```

Sourdough asks an OpenAI-compatible model for a plan, validates it against `resources/plan.schema.json`, and prints it. The model kneads the dough, but you decide when the loaf is ready to bake: if the answer is not valid JSON, does not match the schema, or the model gives up after one retry, Sourdough refuses with a message pointing you to `--plan=<file>` (exit `1`). You write the plan yourself and pass it in.

To see the plan as JSON without writing anything:

```
sourdough new --describe "A blog with posts and comments" --plan-only
```

`--describe` stops at the plan: baking straight from a description is not built yet. Save the plan to a file and pass it with `--plan`, which bakes it:

```
sourdough new my-app --plan plan.json
```

`--plan` reads the file, validates it against the schema, and continues the normal generation flow using the plan's permutation and name. A YAML plan (`.yaml` or `.yml`) works the same way, and the bake saves the plan as [the saved plan](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-saved-plan).

#### Model configuration[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#model-configuration)

`--describe` needs three environment variables (no defaults, no key in code):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_BASE_URL` | the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including the API path (usually `/v1`) |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` | the API key |
| `SOURDOUGH_LLM_MODEL` | the model name |

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works: a hosted API, a local server, or WarriorGPT. Sourdough does not care about the hostname; it only needs the base URL, key, and model.

Danger

`SOURDOUGH_LLM_API_KEY` is a secret. It has no default, and there is no key in code: set it in the environment for the run.

### The steps plan[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#the-steps-plan)

The app plan is the what: permutation, parts, name, models, pages. The steps plan in `src/Plan.php` is the how, that is, what `sourdough new` will do, and `--dry-run` prints it. It carries the permutation, the target dir, and a list of steps:

| Condition | Step |
| --- | --- |
| raw permutation | `Copy the raw template into <dir>` |
| raw permutation | `Replace {{app_name}} and {{app_slug}} in file names and contents` |
| raw-vue permutation | `Copy the raw template, then the raw-vue template over it, into <dir>` |
| raw-vue permutation | `Replace {{app_name}} and {{app_slug}} in file names and contents` |
| any Laravel permutation | `Create the <label> app in <dir>` |
| ADVISOR wired in | `Wire ADVISOR into the app` |
| `--sail` | `Use Sail for the local runtime (compose.yaml, laravel/sail in require-dev)` |
| `--docker` | `Use Docker for the local runtime (Dockerfile, compose.yaml, MySQL 8.4)` |

`--sail` and `--docker` are for the Laravel paths: the raw paths run on plain PHP, and combining either flag with a raw permutation is refused.

### Related[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/plan-format.html#related)

- [Commands](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Wiring the stack in](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wiring-the-stack.html)

---

Source: https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html

## Proof[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says what each check of Sourdough proves and how to run it. Sourdough's promise is that every shape it bakes works on the day it comes out of the oven, so the proof is not a unit test of the generator: it bakes every shape for real, with this checkout, and makes the loaf prove itself.

### Last run[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Run | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh raw` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 25 of 25 steps; suite: 11 tests, 21 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 update | 18 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh raw-vue` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 28 of 28 steps; suite: 16 tests, 34 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 update | 16 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 27 of 27 steps; suite: 9 tests, 17 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update | 27 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade-vue` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 30 of 30 steps; suite: 9 tests, 18 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update | 15 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh inertia` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 31 of 31 steps; suite: 9 tests, 32 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update | 31 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade --sail` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 22 of 22 steps; suite: 9 tests, 17 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 1 record | 11 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade --docker` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 24 of 24 steps; suite: 9 tests, 17 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 5 record | 12 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade-vue --sail` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 22 of 22 steps; suite: 9 tests, 18 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 1 record | 10 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh blade-vue --docker` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 24 of 24 steps; suite: 9 tests, 18 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 5 record | 10 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh inertia --sail` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 22 of 22 steps; suite: 9 tests, 32 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 1 record | 10 s |
| `sh scripts/smoke-shape.sh inertia --docker` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1` | pass: 24 of 24 steps; suite: 9 tests, 32 assertions; fed from 0.1.6: 1 add, 2 update, 5 record | 11 s |
| `composer ci` | 2026-11-07 | `af71db1 + local edits` | pass: 372 tests, 3597 assertions, 2 PHP warnings from older tests; Pint, PHPStan, Squire copy, agent-ready, docs site, audit clean | 369 s |

The `composer ci` row ran in `composer:2.10.3` on PHP 8.5. All eleven proof runs came from one `.\scripts\proof.ps1` on Windows (Docker Desktop, amd64), 178 seconds in all, in the smoke image: PHP 8.5.12, Composer 2.10.3, Node 22.23.4. Templates have changed since 0.1.6 (the platform pin, the resolver refresh, the skeleton tests), so every feed found work: the raw shapes took one update (`composer.json`), the Laravel shapes one add (`tests/Feature/SkeletonTest.php`) and two updates (`app/Sesame/UserResolver.php`, `composer.json`), and the oven runs recorded the scaffold's own files besides (`compose.yaml` for Sail, the `Dockerfile` and its friends for Docker), because a 0.1.6 manifest never named them. The oven feeds also crossed the 0.1.6 gap where the manifest hashed `composer.json` before the scaffold edited it: feed rebuilt the missing base from the app's file and merged from it (see [What it found](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-found)). The Laravel shapes ship nine tests each now: the two starter examples plus seven skeleton tests covering `/up`, the home page, the sign-in redirect, the signed-in dashboard, a 404 and the user refresh; the count is theirs, not the proof's.

### What it found[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-found)

The first run of the harness, on the same day, failed nine of eleven runs. Six of the failures were Sourdough's:

- **An app baked by 0.1.6 with `--sail` or `--docker` could never feed cleanly.** 0.1.6 wrote the manifest before the oven's scaffold ran, so it named no oven and hashed `composer.json` before the scaffold edited it. `sourdough feed` then baked the plain shape, called the app fresh and wrote nothing, and `sourdough manifest --check` reported `composer.json` changed for good. Fixed in the same branch: feed reads the oven from the app's files when a 0.1.6 manifest names none, and a new `record` action moves the manifest to a file the app already has right ([Keeping apps current](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/keeping-current.html#what-feed-does)).
- The other three failures were the harness's own: Laravel's router wants `public/` as its working directory. Fixed before the run above, along with the suite count, which Pest prints in color even without a terminal.

Still open, from the same runs:

- **The raw shapes run PROCTOR on its bundled policy**, the Laravel shapes on CREED's released one. No shape's `proctor` script passes `--policy` any more (PROCTOR 0.6 refuses it in CI): the Laravel shapes require `waynestate/creed`, and PROCTOR reads its policy from `vendor/waynestate/creed` by itself; the raw template does not require it.
- **PROCTOR warns `php-floor`** on every shape: PHP 8.3 is in security-only support until 2027-12-31. Expected, and the stack's floor until then.

The run above closed the last failure, in all six oven runs: **a 0.1.6 oven bake conflicted on `composer.json` at its first feed after a template change.** 0.1.6 hashed `composer.json` before the oven's scaffold edited it, so the manifest named a version no checkout ever held: the app's file carried the scaffold's edits, and the base for a three-way merge was nowhere, not in `.sourdough/base/` (first feed) and not in the app's git history (the pre-scaffold version was never committed). While the template's `composer.json` stayed the same as 0.1.6's, the post-scaffold files matched and nothing happened; once the template's file changed (this cycle, the platform pin), feed marked both versions and stopped. Feed now rebuilds that base: it undoes the scaffold's edit to recover the pre-scaffold composer data, verifies the data against the recorded hash, and reapplies the scaffold to get the exact file the app started from. An oven app that never touched `composer.json` takes the template's as an update, and a real app edit still merges over the rebuilt base, or conflicts as before. All eleven runs pass.

### Run it[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it)

The proof harness is a pair: `scripts/proof.sh` on Linux and macOS, `scripts/proof.ps1` on Windows. Both build the smoke image (`scripts/smoke.Dockerfile`: PHP 8.5, Composer 2.10.3, Node 22, pinned) and run every bake inside it, one after another, so the result is the same on every machine.

sh

```bash
sh scripts/proof.sh            # every run
sh scripts/proof.sh raw inertia+docker
```

PowerShell

```powershell
.\scripts\proof.ps1            # every run
.\scripts\proof.ps1 raw inertia+docker -OutDir C:\temp\proof
```

It needs git and Docker, and the network for Composer, npm, Packagist and the WayneUI release. It needs no credentials: every bake passes `--no-playbook` and `--no-advisor`, and the gate drops any Oracle, CAS or Composer credential the host leaks in.

The harness proofs the committed tree plus any edits to tracked files (`git stash create`), never untracked files, and the table marks the commit `+ local edits` when there were any. The source goes into the container as one tar file from `git archive` rather than a mounted folder, because Docker Desktop can list a mounted folder only partially. `git archive` honors the `export-ignore` lines in `.gitattributes`, so the proof bakes with the package exactly as Composer ships it: no tests, no site, no `composer.lock`, and Sourdough's own dependencies resolve fresh, as they do for anyone who installs it from Packagist. The CI job runs on the checkout instead, lock and all.

Results land in `proof-out/` (or `-OutDir`, or `PROOF_OUT`):

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `last-run.md` | the table above, ready to paste |
| `summary.txt` | the image's versions, one line per run, the total |
| `logs/<run>.txt` | the run's `ok` and `FAIL` lines |
| `logs/<run>/<n>.log` | the full output of each step |

The exit code is `0` when every run passed, `1` when any failed, `2` when the harness could not start. To refresh this page, run the harness on a clean checkout of `main` and paste `last-run.md` over the table.

| Setting | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| runs (arguments) | `raw`, `raw-vue`, `blade`, `blade-vue`, `inertia`, or a Laravel shape in an oven: `blade+sail`, `blade+docker`, `blade-vue+sail`, `blade-vue+docker`, `inertia+sail`, `inertia+docker`. None means all eleven. |
| `PROOF_FEED_FROM` (`-FeedFrom`) | the released Sourdough to feed forward from. Default: the newest release in `CHANGELOG.md`; `none` skips the feed. |
| `PROOF_OUT` (`-OutDir`) | where the results go. Default: `proof-out/`. |
| `--here` | `proof.sh` only: run in this machine instead of Docker. The CI job uses it inside the smoke image. |

### What each run proves[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-each-run-proves)

Every run goes through `scripts/smoke-shape.sh`, the same gate the per-shape smoke jobs run on every pipeline. Each step prints `ok` or `FAIL`; the first `FAIL` stops the run and shows the step's tail.

1. **It bakes.** `sourdough new` with this checkout's own CLI, so the starter under test is the one being shipped.
2. **The manifest is clean.** `sourdough manifest --check` exits 0 right after the bake: every managed file matches `.sourdough/manifest.json`.
3. **The bake is reproducible.** The fresh app is committed to a scratch git repository and `sourdough feed --dry-run` must find nothing to feed. A loaf that came out different every time would make every feed of it a conflict.
4. **Yesterday's loaf feeds forward.** The same shape is baked with the last release, installed from Packagist, and committed as an app would be. This checkout's `sourdough feed` must bring it up to date without a conflict, `sourdough manifest --check` must be clean afterwards, and a second `sourdough feed --dry-run` must find nothing left to do.
5. **It installs.** `composer install` (and `npm ci --ignore-scripts` for the Vue shapes) from the baked `composer.json` and the shipped `package-lock.json`.
6. **Its own suite passes.** `composer test` for the raw shapes (PHPUnit), `php artisan test` for the Laravel shapes (Pest 4). The table quotes the suite's own count.
7. **PROCTOR passes.** `composer proctor`: the stack's checks against CREED's policy, from inside the app.
8. **Its own gate passes.** `composer ci`, plus `npm run build` for the Vue shapes and `npm run typecheck` for Inertia.
9. **It serves.** A live server, then its front page:

| Shape | Server | `/` must answer 200 with | Also |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raw PHP | `php -S` with `APP_ENV=local`, after fetching the pinned WayneUI release into `public/wayne-ui.php` | `app is running.` in WayneUI's shell | `/nope` 404, `/up` 200 |
| Raw PHP + Vue | the same | the built app (`src="/build/assets/`) mounted on `id="app"` | `/api/me` 401 without a session and the fake user with one, `/nope` 404 with the app, `/up` 200 |
| Laravel + Blade | `php -S` with Laravel's own router, as `php artisan serve` runs it | `baked fresh by Sourdough` | `/dashboard` signs in with SESAME's fake driver, `/nope` 404, `/up` 200 |
| Laravel + Blade + Vue islands | the same | `baked fresh by Sourdough` and the built assets | `/dashboard` carries the `data-vue-island="counter"` island, `/nope` 404, `/up` 200 |
| Laravel + Inertia/Vue | the same | the `Home` page component and the built assets | `/dashboard` renders the `Dashboard` page after the fake sign-in, `/nope` 404, `/up` 200 |

#### The ovens[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#the-ovens)

A Laravel shape with `--sail` or `--docker` is proven up to the oven door. The run bakes it, checks the manifest, the reproducible bake and the feed from the last release as above, checks that the scaffold wrote its files (`compose.yaml` and `laravel/sail` for Sail; the `Dockerfile`, `compose.yaml`, `.dockerignore` and the `dev-up` script for Docker), then installs the app and runs its own suite and PROCTOR. The oven's `.env.example` points at MySQL, which the gate does not run; the suite keeps to SQLite in memory, as `phpunit.xml` says.

### composer ci[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#composer-ci)

Sourdough's own gate, the same command on GitLab and GitHub:

```sh
composer ci   # validate, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan, the Squire copy, agent-ready files, the docs site, audit
```

The PHPUnit suite covers every generator, the manifest, `sourdough feed` on every shape with local edits, merges, conflicts and refusals (`tests/FeedCommandTest.php`, offline), and the Sail and Docker scaffolds file by file. `tests/ProofHarnessTest.php` keeps the two harness scripts, the gate, the CI job and the table on this page listing the same runs.

### On CI[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#on-ci)

Each shape's smoke job (`smoke-raw`, `smoke-raw-vue`, `smoke-blade`, `smoke-blade-vue`, `smoke-inertia`) runs the gate on every pipeline, without the feed from the last release and without the ovens.

The `proof` job runs the whole harness. It never runs on a push: start it by hand from any pipeline, or from a pipeline schedule that sets `SOURDOUGH_PROOF` to `1`. It keeps `proof-out/` (the table, the summary and every step log) as an artifact for 30 days. Like the smoke jobs it is allowed to fail for now. The runner it lands on is arm64 where the table above ran on amd64, so a green `proof` job is the arm64 half of the same proof.

Tip

Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so the proof and every app's pipeline run where the code lives.

### What it does not prove yet[#](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-does-not-prove-yet)

- **No oven is lit.** The `--sail` and `--docker` runs never start a compose stack: the gate has no Docker daemon. The scaffold tests (`tests/SailScaffoldTest.php`, `tests/DockerScaffoldTest.php`) pin their files.
- **No Playbook, no ADVISOR.** Every bake passes `--no-playbook` (its package is private and the proof runs credential-free) and `--no-advisor`. A Wayne State app needs Playbook; its wiring is covered by the unit suite.
- **No MySQL or Oracle.** The Laravel shapes migrate SQLite; nothing connects to a database server.
- **No browser.** The front page is fetched with curl. Nothing clicks the Vue island, runs axe on a baked app, or checks it on a phone.
- **A feed with local edits** is proven by `tests/FeedCommandTest.php`, not by the harness: the harness feeds an app nobody has touched.

- [Testing](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/testing.html)
